definition_zh: 层；层次；地层；涂层；产蛋鸡
definition_en: a thickness or sheet of material covering a surface; one of several levels in a system; a hen that lays eggs
core_image: 一张一张薄片叠起来，像千层饼的横截面，每一层都清晰可数
scene: 地质课上，老师用铲子切开岩壁，露出水平排列的一层层岩石。他指着说： Each layer was laid down in a different age.
sceneCN: 这里 layer 是「岩层、地层」（第 3 个义项：地质沉积层）；句意：每一层岩石都是在不同年代沉积下来的。图中可辨识物件：岩壁、铲子、水平岩层、地质锤。

derivatives.zh: 分层的；有层次的
分层；层叠；压条繁殖
多层的；多层结构
夹层；中间层

senses.title: A sheet laid over a surface
senses.titleCN: 铺在表面上的一层：涂层、薄层
senses.definition: a thickness or sheet of material that covers a surface
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖在表面上的一层材料或一片物质
senses.example: A thin layer of dust covered the table.
senses.exampleCN: 桌上覆盖着一层薄薄的灰。
senses.why: Layer is lay + -er: 'that which is laid'. A layer is material placed down on a surface, seen as one sheet rather than as a mass.
senses.whyCN: layer 是 lay 加 -er，即“被铺下的东西”。一层就是把材料铺在表面上，被看作一片，而不是一团。

senses.title: One level in a stack of levels
senses.titleCN: 层层结构中的一级：层次
senses.definition: one of several levels in a system, idea or organization, each built on or above another
senses.definitionCN: 系统、思想或组织中的若干层级之一，每一层建立在另一层之上
senses.example: The novel works on several layers of meaning.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说在好几层意义上成立。
senses.why: Anything that can be laid down one piece over another can be imagined as a stack. Ideas and organizations borrow the physical stack and call each level a layer.
senses.whyCN: 任何能一层压一层铺放的东西，都可以被想象成一摞。思想与组织借用这个物理堆叠，把每一级称为一层。

senses.title: A stratum in the earth
senses.definition: in geology, a band of rock or soil of one kind, deposited at a particular period
senses.definitionCN: 地质学中，某一时期沉积形成的同一种岩石或土壤带
senses.example: The fossils were found in a layer of limestone.
senses.exampleCN: 化石是在一层石灰岩中发现的。
senses.why: Sediment settles in sheets, one age on top of another. Geology sees the earth's history as a stack of layers, so the word becomes a technical term for a stratum.
senses.whyCN: 沉积物一片一片落下，一个年代压在另一个年代上。地质学把地球历史看成一摞层，于是这个词成为“地层”的术语。

senses.title: A band around the planet
senses.titleCN: 包围地球的一带：大气层
senses.definition: in geography, a distinct band of the atmosphere or ocean at a particular height or depth
senses.definitionCN: 地理学中，大气或海洋在特定高度或深度上的一条明显带
senses.example: The ozone layer protects us from harmful radiation.
senses.exampleCN: 臭氧层保护我们免受有害辐射。
senses.why: The atmosphere is arranged in shells, one above another. Each shell is a layer because it can be drawn as a band laid over the one below.
senses.whyCN: 大气按壳层排列，一层在另一层之上。每个壳层都是一层，因为它可以被画成覆盖在下面那层上的一条带。

senses.title: A level in software
senses.titleCN: 软件中的一层：分层架构
senses.definition: in computing, one level of a system or protocol that communicates with the levels above and below it
senses.definitionCN: 计算机中，与上下层通信的系统或协议的一级
senses.example: The application layer sits above the network layer.
senses.exampleCN: 应用层位于网络层之上。
senses.why: Software designers picture a system as a stack of levels, each hiding the details of the one below. The physical stack of sheets becomes an architecture.
senses.whyCN: 软件设计者把系统想象成一摞层级，每一层隐藏下面一层的细节。物理的薄片堆叠变成了架构。

senses.title: One coat of paint
senses.definition: one application or coat of paint, varnish or another covering material
senses.definitionCN: 油漆、清漆或其他覆盖材料的一次涂布
senses.example: The wall needs two more layers of paint.
senses.exampleCN: 这面墙还需要再刷两层漆。
senses.why: Painting is the most literal act of laying down a sheet of material. Each pass adds one more layer, and the old surface disappears under it.
senses.whyCN: 刷漆是最字面的“铺下一层材料”。每刷一遍就多一层，旧表面被盖在下面。

senses.title: Clothing stacked for warmth
senses.titleCN: 为保暖叠穿：一层层衣物
senses.definition: one garment or set of garments worn over another, especially for warmth
senses.definitionCN: 穿在另一件外面的一件或多件衣物，尤为了保暖
senses.example: Wear several thin layers instead of one thick coat.
senses.exampleCN: 穿几层薄衣服，而不是一件厚外套。
senses.why: Dressing in layers is stacking sheets of fabric around the body. Each garment is a layer, and warmth comes from the trapped air between them.
senses.whyCN: 分层穿衣就是把一片片布料叠在身体周围。每件衣服是一层，温暖来自层与层之间被困住的空气。

senses.title: The hen that lays
senses.definition: a hen kept for laying eggs, or a hen that lays eggs regularly
senses.definitionCN: 为产蛋而饲养的母鸡，或定期下蛋的母鸡
senses.example: The farm keeps two hundred layers.
senses.exampleCN: 这个农场养了两百只产蛋鸡。
senses.why: This is the agent sense of -er: a layer is 'one who lays'. It is not a sheet at all, but the same suffix that names the one performing the action.
senses.whyCN: 这是 -er 的施动者义：layer 就是“下蛋的那一个”。它完全不是薄片，而是同一个后缀用来命名执行动作的主体。

senses.title: Layering a plant
senses.titleCN: 压条繁殖：layer 的园艺动词
senses.definition: in gardening, to make a stem root while still attached to the parent plant, or the resulting rooted branch
senses.definitionCN: 园艺中使枝条在仍连着母株时生根，或指这样生根的枝条
senses.example: They layered the rose bush to produce a new plant.
senses.exampleCN: 他们对这株玫瑰进行压条，以培育新植株。
senses.why: The gardener bends a stem down and 'lays' it under soil. The new plant is produced by a laying-down, so the method and the verb share the original physical action.
senses.whyCN: 园丁把枝条弯下并“铺”在土里。新植株由一次“铺下”产生，所以这种方法与动词共享最初的物理动作。

intro.en: Layer is an English agent noun: lay + -er, 'one who or that which lays'. Lay goes back to Old English lecgan 'to place', from the causative of the verb that became lie. The 'sheet of material' sense developed later, probably under some influence from French cookery terms.
intro.cn: layer 是英语的施动名词：lay 加 -er，即“放置的人或物”。lay 可追溯到古英语 lecgan“放置”，它是后来变成 lie 的动词的使役形式。“一层材料”的义项发展较晚，可能受到法语烹饪用语的一些影响。

items.en: The root *legh- meant 'to lie down, lay'. It underlies English lie, lay and law (something 'laid down'), and German liegen and legen.
items.cn: 词根 *legh- 意为“躺下、放下”。它是英语 lie、lay 和 law（“被放下的东西”）以及德语 liegen、legen 的深层来源。

items.en: Lecgan meant 'to place on the ground or another surface; place in order; put down'. It was the causative of licgan 'to lie': to lay is to cause to lie.
items.cn: lecgan 意为“放在地上或其他表面上；按顺序摆放；放下”。它是 licgan“躺”的使役形式：lay 就是“使……躺下”。

items.en: Layer is first recorded in the late 14th century as 'one who or that lays', especially a mason who lays stones. This is the agent-noun sense of -er.
items.cn: layer 最早记录于 14 世纪晚期，意为“放置的人或物”，尤指砌石的泥瓦匠。这是 -er 的施动名词义。

items.en: The passive sense 'a thickness of material laid over a surface' is recorded by the 1610s. Because the earliest English uses were in cookery, the sense may have been influenced by French liue 'binding', a word used of a thickened sauce.
items.cn: 被动义“铺在表面上的一层材料”记录于 17 世纪 10 年代。由于英语最早的用法出现在烹饪中，这个义项可能受到法语 liue“黏合”的影响，后者用于浓稠酱汁。

items.en: The hen sense 'a hen that lays eggs' is recorded by 1707. Layer cake is attested from 1875, naming a cake made of stacked layers.
items.cn: “下蛋的母鸡”义项记录于 1707 年。layer cake（千层蛋糕）记录于 1875 年，指由叠层制成的蛋糕。

items.en: The verb layer is from 1779 in horticulture, as a method of plant propagation. The general sense 'form into layers' is attested by 1852.
items.cn: 动词 layer 来自 1779 年的园艺用法，指一种植物繁殖方法。“形成层”的一般义项记录于 1852 年。

note.en: The look-alike group is the lay/layer family; the near-meaning group contains words for sheets and levels, each from a different material or scale.
note.cn: 形近组是 lay/layer 词族；近义组是薄片与层级类词，各自的材料或尺度不同。

entries.definition: to put something down on a surface; to place in order. It is the verb behind layer, and its past tense is laid, not layed.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物放在表面上；按顺序摆放。它是 layer 背后的动词，过去式是 laid，不是 layed。

entries.definition: the act of putting something down, or of a hen producing an egg. It is the -ing form of lay.
entries.definitionCN: 放下某物的动作，或母鸡下蛋。它是 lay 的 -ing 形式。

entries.definition: arranged in layers, or having several levels. The past participle became an adjective describing a stacked structure.
entries.definitionCN: 分层排列的，或具有多个层次的。过去分词变成形容词，描述堆叠结构。

entries.definition: a layer of rock or soil, especially one of many deposited in sequence. It is the technical Latin word for a geological layer.
entries.definitionCN: 岩石或土壤的一层，尤指按顺序沉积的许多层之一。它是地质层的拉丁技术词。

entries.definition: a thin layer of a substance covering a surface. It stresses the material spread over something, often for protection.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖在表面上的一薄层物质。它强调铺在表面的材料，常带保护目的。

entries.definition: a very thin layer or membrane. It is thinner than a typical layer and often continuous and transparent.
entries.definitionCN: 极薄的一层或膜。它比一般的 layer 更薄，常是连续而透明的。

entries.definition: one of several levels in a hierarchy, especially when they are ranked. It is the social or organizational counterpart of a physical layer.
entries.definitionCN: 等级体系中的一层，尤指被排序的层级。它是物理 layer 在社会或组织中的对应词。

normalIntro.en: Real pieces only: lay 'place down' + -er, plus the ordinary family layered, layering, multilayer, interlayer. The 'sheet' sense came later than the 'one who lays' sense.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实构件：lay“放下”加 -er，以及常用词族 layered、layering、multilayer、interlayer。“薄层”义晚于“放置者”义出现。

normal.en: Layer = lay + -er. The first meaning was 'one who lays', like a mason laying stones; only later did it mean 'that which is laid' as a sheet.
normal.cn: layer = lay + -er。最早的意思是“放置者”，像砌石的泥瓦匠；后来才表示“被铺下的东西”，即一层。

normal.en: A hen that lays eggs is also a layer, because -er can name the doer. The same suffix gives both the mason and the sheet.
normal.cn: 下蛋的母鸡也是 layer，因为 -er 可以命名动作的执行者。同一个后缀既给出泥瓦匠，也给出薄层。

normal.en: A geological layer is history stacked: each sheet of sediment is an older page under a newer one.
normal.cn: 地层就是被叠起来的历史：每一片沉积物都是压在更新一页下面的旧页。

normal.en: In computing, a layer hides the layer below it. The stack is physical in origin and architectural in use.
normal.cn: 在计算机中，一层隐藏下面一层。这个堆叠起源于物理，却被用于架构。

normal.en: Fixed patterns: a thin layer of, the ozone layer, layers of meaning, and in layers.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：a thin layer of（薄薄一层）、the ozone layer（臭氧层）、layers of meaning（层层含义）、in layers（分层地）。

abstract.en: A layer is both a cover and a record: it hides what is below while preserving it.
abstract.cn: 一层既是覆盖，也是记录：它遮住下面的东西，同时把它保存下来。

abstract.en: Complexity is often just depth: when a thing has too many layers, we stop seeing the surface and start seeing a system.
abstract.cn: 复杂往往只是深度：当一个东西层数太多，我们就不再看到表面，而开始看到一个系统。

abstract.en: Every layer was laid by someone or something. The word keeps the action inside the noun, which is why a stratum can be read as a date.
abstract.cn: 每一层都是由某个力量铺下的。这个词把动作保留在名词里，所以一层地层可以被读成一个年代。

examples.en: A thick layer of snow covered the car.
examples.cn: 厚厚的一层雪盖住了汽车。

examples.en: The problem has several layers that must be solved separately.
examples.cn: 这个问题有几层，必须分别解决。

examples.en: The farmer keeps a hundred layers for eggs.
examples.cn: 农场主养了一百只产蛋鸡。

dict_mnemonic.text: “累·尔”——累（了就把）尔（等薄片）一层层叠起来 → layer 层

root: 由英语动词 lay“放下、铺下”加施动后缀 -er 构成；lay 源于古英语 lecgan“放置”，再上溯到原始印欧语 *legh-“躺下、放下”，核心是“被铺下去的一片”，也保留“放置者”的施动义。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of layer, all one action: something is laid down on something else. Dust, meaning, rock, atmosphere, software, paint, clothing, a laying hen and a propagated stem each come from that same verb lay.
sensesIntro.cn: layer 的九个义项都是同一个动作：某物被铺在另一物上。灰尘、意义、岩石、大气、软件、油漆、衣物、下蛋的母鸡和压条的枝条，都来自同一个动词 lay。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: thin sheets stacked one on another, each visible as a separate band.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张张薄片叠在一起，每一片都能被看成分明的一带。

branches.en: MATERIAL LAID ON A SURFACE: dust, paint and clothing are added as sheets over what is already there.
branches.cn: 铺在表面上的材料：灰尘、油漆和衣物都是一片片加在已有之物上面。

branches.en: LEVELS IN A SYSTEM: meanings and software are built as stacks, each level resting on another.
branches.cn: 系统中的层级：意义与软件都以堆叠方式建立，每一层依托另一层。

branches.en: NATURAL BANDS: rock strata record ages, and atmospheric shells wrap the planet in bands.
branches.cn: 自然界的层带：岩层记录年代，大气壳层以带状包裹地球。

branches.en: THE DOER: a laying hen is a layer because -er can name the one performing the action.
branches.cn: 执行者：下蛋的母鸡是 layer，因为 -er 可以命名执行动作的主体。

branches.en: THE HORTICULTURAL ACT: a stem is laid under soil so that it roots, turning the verb back into a physical laying-down.
branches.cn: 园艺动作：枝条被铺在土下以便生根，使动词回到物理上的“铺下”。

intro.en: Layer is an English compound of lay + -er. Its family is built with -ed, -ing, and the prefixes multi- and inter-.
intro.cn: layer 是 lay + -er 的英语复合词。它的词族用 -ed、-ing，以及前缀 multi-、inter- 构成。

latinIntro.en: Layer has no Latin root; it is native English. The Latin word for a geological layer is stratum, from sternere 'to spread out', which is a useful contrast rather than a source.
latinIntro.cn: layer 没有拉丁词根，是本族英语词。地质层的拉丁词是 stratum，来自 sternere“铺开”，这是有用的对照，而不是来源。

items.meaning: a sheet laid over a surface; one who lays
items.meaningCN: 层；放置者（-er 表施动者或事物）
items.example: A layer of ice formed on the pond.

items.meaning: several sheets or levels; the act of layering
items.meaningCN: 多层；分层（复数或第三人称单数）

items.example: The story has a layered structure.

items.meaning: the act of arranging in layers; plant propagation
items.example: Layering is a simple way to propagate plants.
items.exampleCN: 压条是一种简单的植物繁殖方法。
这种薄膜使用多层包装。

items.meaningCN: 夹层；中间层（inter- 表之间）
items.example: A thin interlayer separates the two sheets.
items.exampleCN: 一层薄薄的夹层把两片材料隔开。

items.meaning: a cake made of stacked layers
items.example: She baked a chocolate layer cake.
items.exampleCN: 她烤了一个巧克力千层蛋糕。

items.meaning: the atmospheric band rich in ozone
items.example: The ozone layer absorbs ultraviolet light.

items.meaningCN: 放置；铺下（layer 的基础动词）
items.example: She laid the cloth on the table.

latinEntries.meaning: a layer, bed, pavement (not the source of layer)
latinEntries.meaningCN: 层；地层（并非 layer 的来源，仅作对照）

latinEntries.meaning: bed, couch (same PIE root as lay)
latinEntries.meaningCN: 床；卧榻（与 lay 同出一个原始印欧语词根）

definition_zh: 张力；紧张；拉力
definition_en: a stretched state, or a feeling of worry and strain between people
core_image: 一根被拉到极限、随时会断的绳
scene: 谈判桌上谁都不说话。 The rope was stretched until the tension could be felt.
sceneCN: 这里 tension 是「拉力、张力」（第 1 个义项：被拉伸的状态）；句意：绳子被拉紧到能感觉到张力。

derivatives.zh: 由同一词根 tens- 构成，义为「绷紧的」
tense 加副词后缀，义为「紧张地」
tension 加否定后缀，义为「无张力的」

senses.title: A stretched state
senses.definition: the state of being stretched tight
senses.definitionCN: 被拉紧的状态
senses.example: The tension in the rope held the bridge steady.
senses.exampleCN: 绳子的张力让桥保持稳定。
senses.why: The Latin root tendere means to stretch, so a stretched thing carries force.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 tendere 意为「拉伸」，被拉伸的东西就带着力。

senses.title: A feeling of strain
senses.definition: a nervous, worried feeling
senses.definitionCN: 紧张、不安的情绪
senses.example: She felt the tension rise before the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 考试前她感到紧张加剧。
senses.why: A mind stretched by worry works like a rope stretched by force.
senses.whyCN: 被焦虑「拉伸」的心，就像被外力拉紧的绳。

senses.title: Strained relations
senses.definition: a situation where people or countries distrust each other
senses.definitionCN: 人与人或国与国之间互不信任的局势
senses.example: Trade talks reduced the tension between the two nations.
senses.exampleCN: 贸易会谈缓解了两国间的紧张。
senses.why: Distrust pulls people apart the way force pulls a rope.
senses.whyCN: 不信任把人拉开，正如外力把绳拉开。

intro.en: Tension comes from Latin tendere, to stretch.
intro.cn: tension 源自拉丁语 tendere（拉伸）。

items.en: Tendere meant to stretch or extend.
items.cn: tendere 意为拉伸、延展。

items.en: Tensio described the act of stretching.
items.cn: tensio 描述拉伸的动作。

items.en: The word passed through French as tension.
items.cn: 该词经法语 tension 传入。

items.en: Tension first meant physical stretching.
items.cn: tension 最初指物理上的拉伸。

items.en: The sense extended to nervous and social strain.
items.cn: 词义扩展到心理与社会的紧张。

note.en: Tension is compared with look-alike words and with words for strain.
note.cn: 把 tension 与形近词及表示紧张的词作对比。

entries.definition: a cord joining muscle to bone
tight or nervous
not a standard English word
entries.definitionCN: 非标准拼写；只是拼写相近

entries.definition: pressure or worry
too much effort or worry
entries.definitionCN: 过度劳累；与 tension 同根

entries.definition: a strong worried feeling
entries.definitionCN: 焦虑；只表情绪，不表拉力

normalIntro.en: Tension is a rope pulled tight, in the body or between nations.
normalIntro.cn: tension 是一根拉紧的绳，存在于身体里，也存在于国家之间。

normal.en: The tension in the wire kept the tent firm.
normal.cn: 钢丝的张力让帐篷稳固。

normal.en: She felt tension in her shoulders.
normal.cn: 她感到肩部紧张。

normal.en: Ease the tension before the meeting.
normal.cn: 开会前先缓和紧张气氛。

normal.en: Surface tension lets insects walk on water.
normal.cn: 表面张力让昆虫能在水面行走。

normal.en: The tension between the teams was obvious.
normal.cn: 两队之间的紧张显而易见。

abstract.en: A stretched rope is a worried mind.
abstract.cn: 拉紧的绳，就是忧心的人。

abstract.en: Force held but not released is tension.
abstract.cn: 被压住却没释放的力，就是张力。

abstract.en: What pulls apart creates strain.
abstract.cn: 把东西拉开的，就制造紧张。

examples.en: The tension in the rope held the bridge steady.
examples.cn: 绳子的张力让桥保持稳定。

examples.en: She felt the tension rise before the exam.
examples.cn: 考试前她感到紧张加剧。

examples.en: Trade talks reduced the tension between the two nations.
examples.cn: 贸易会谈缓解了两国间的紧张。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ten·伸」——绳被「拉伸」到极限，张力满满，人也跟着紧张。

root: 拉丁语 tendere（拉伸）派生名词 tensio，经古法语进入英语，由「拉伸之力」引申为「紧张」。

sensesIntro.en: Tension moves from a stretched rope to a stretched mind and strained relations.
sensesIntro.cn: tension 从被拉紧的绳，延伸到紧绷的心和紧张的关系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rope pulled to its limit.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根拉到极限的绳。

branches.en: Physical stretching is the base sense.
branches.cn: 物理拉伸是基础义项。

branches.en: A stretched mind feels nervous.
branches.cn: 被拉伸的心会紧张。

branches.en: Inner worry and outer distrust mirror each other.
branches.cn: 内心的忧虑与外在的不信任互为映照。

branches.en: Surface tension holds water films together.
branches.cn: 表面张力把水膜绷在一起。

branches.en: Talks release the pull between rivals.
branches.cn: 会谈释放对手之间的拉力。

intro.en: Tension extends through the tend- family and common suffixes.
intro.cn: tension 通过 tend- 词族与常见后缀扩展。

latinIntro.en: Tension traces to Latin tendere, to stretch.
latinIntro.cn: tension 可追溯到拉丁语 tendere（拉伸）。

items.meaning: a cord joining muscle to bone
items.example: The tendon links muscle and bone.

definition_zh: 结论；结尾；结束；缔结
definition_en: a judgment reached after thinking, or the end of something
core_image: 一篇文章最后一个句号落下的瞬间
scene: 论文写到最后一页，他把所有线索收进一段话。 The conclusion ties together every thread of the argument.
sceneCN: 这里 conclusion 指「结尾部分」（第 2 个义项：文章或讲话的最后一段）；句意是结尾把论证的每一条线索都收拢起来。

derivatives.zh: 断定；结束
决定性的；确凿的
确凿地
无定论的

senses.title: A judgment reached
senses.definition: a decision or opinion formed after considering the facts
senses.definitionCN: 在考虑事实之后形成的决定或看法
senses.example: Her conclusion was based on solid evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 她的结论建立在确凿证据之上。
senses.why: When the reasoning is closed, what remains is the conclusion.
senses.whyCN: 推理合上之后，留下来的就是结论。

senses.title: The end of something
senses.definition: the final part or end of an event or piece of writing
senses.definitionCN: 事件或文章的最后部分或终点
senses.example: The conclusion of the speech was moving.
senses.exampleCN: 演讲的结尾很动人。
senses.why: The last part closes the whole, just as a lid closes a box.
senses.whyCN: 最后一部分合上整体，正如盖子合上箱子。

senses.title: A formal agreement
senses.definition: the act of completing a treaty or deal formally
senses.definitionCN: 正式完成条约或交易的行为
senses.example: The conclusion of the peace treaty was welcomed.
senses.exampleCN: 和平条约的缔结受到欢迎。
senses.why: A deal is brought to its close, and that close is named the conclusion.
senses.whyCN: 交易被带到终点，而那个终点就叫 conclusion。

intro.en: Conclusion comes from Latin conclusio, a closing, from concludere, to shut up together.
intro.cn: conclusion 来自拉丁语 conclusio（关闭），源自动词 concludere（一起关上）。

items.en: Claudere meant to close or to shut.
items.cn: claudere 意为关闭或合上。

items.en: Concludere meant to shut something in or to finish it.
items.cn: concludere 意为把某物关起来或完成它。

items.en: Conclusio named a closing and also a final inference.
items.cn: conclusio 指收尾，也指最终的推论。

items.en: Old French conclusion kept both the ending and the reasoning senses.
items.cn: 古法语 conclusion 同时保留结束与推理两种含义。

items.en: English conclusion first meant the end of a speech or argument.
items.cn: 英语 conclusion 最初指演讲或论证的结尾。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words close in shape to conclusion, and the meaning group names other words for a result or an ending.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 conclusion 形状相近的词，近义组列出其他表示结果与结尾的词。

entries.definition: proving something beyond doubt
a state of not understanding
the act of including something
a decision made by a court or judge
the last part of a story or event
what happens because of something

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a final full stop, then move to the verdict of a court and the closing of a treaty.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从最后一个句号开始，再走到法庭裁决与条约缔结。

normal.en: Conclusion is the noun of conclude, so it is the closed result.
normal.cn: conclusion 是 conclude 的名词，所以它就是被合上的结果。

normal.en: In conclusion means the closing words are coming now.
normal.cn: in conclusion 意为收尾的话现在要来了。

normal.en: A conclusion is a verdict built out of reasons.
normal.cn: 结论是用理由搭建起来的裁决。

normal.en: The conclusion of a treaty is its formal closing.
normal.cn: 条约的 conclusion 就是它正式的缔结。

normal.en: Jump to a conclusion and you close the case too early.
normal.cn: 急于下结论，就是太早合上案卷。

abstract.en: Picture the last full stop landing on a white page.
abstract.cn: 想象最后一个句号落在白纸上。

abstract.en: Picture a judge setting down a folder and looking up.
abstract.cn: 想象法官放下卷宗，抬起头。

abstract.en: Picture two pens signing the final page of a treaty.
abstract.cn: 想象两支笔在条约最后一页签字。

examples.en: The evidence led them to a clear conclusion.
examples.cn: 证据让他们得出了明确的结论。

examples.en: In conclusion, the plan needs more time.
examples.cn: 总之，这个计划需要更多时间。

examples.en: The conclusion of the film left everyone silent.
examples.cn: 电影的结尾让所有人都沉默了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 conclusion 记成 con（一起）加 clus（关闭）加 ion：把事情合起来定下，就是结论与结尾。

root: 源自拉丁语 concludere（com 一起 + claudere 关闭）的名词 conclusio，本义是关闭、收尾，后指结论、结尾与缔结。

sensesIntro.en: From the case being closed on a judgment, to the last page, and finally to a treaty brought to its close.
sensesIntro.cn: 从案卷在判决上合起，到最后一页，最后到被带到终点的条约。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the moment the final full stop lands on the page.
core.cn: 核心意象：最后一个句号落在纸上的瞬间。

branches.en: A judgment is the mental result of closing the argument.
branches.cn: 结论是合上论证之后的思维结果。

branches.en: The ending is the physical last part of a text or event.
branches.cn: 结尾是文章或活动最后的具体部分。

branches.en: A treaty is concluded, and that act is its conclusion.
branches.cn: 条约被缔结，而这一行为就是 conclusion。

branches.en: Reasoning and writing both arrive at a closing point.
branches.cn: 推理与写作都抵达一个收束点。

branches.en: An ending and a sealed deal both refuse further change.
branches.cn: 结尾与封定的交易都拒绝再改。

intro.en: Conclusion is built on Latin com-, together, plus claudere, to close, with the noun ending -sion.
intro.cn: conclusion 由拉丁语 com-（一起）、claudere（关闭）与名词词尾 -sion 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin close base clus- also gives exclusion, inclusion and seclusion.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的关闭词基 clus- 还给出 exclusion、inclusion 与 seclusion。

items.example: The two studies reached different conclusions.
items.exampleCN: 两项研究得出了不同的结论。

items.example: We conclude that the method works.
items.exampleCN: 我们断定这个方法有效。

items.example: There is conclusive proof of the change.
items.exampleCN: 有确凿证据表明这一变化。

items.example: The conclusiveness of the data was debated.
items.exampleCN: 数据的决定性受到争论。

items.example: The deal was concluded in June.

definition_zh: 民主的；有民主精神的；平等的
definition_en: based on the idea that all people have an equal right to choose and to speak
core_image: 一间教室里所有人围坐成一圈，谁都可以举手说话
scene: 班会上老师没有直接定下方案，而是让每个同学先说自己想法。 The club made a democratic decision to share the work equally.
sceneCN: 这里 democratic 指「民主的」（第 1 个义项：由众人平等参与决定的）；句意是这个社团以民主方式决定平分工作。

pos.zh: 民主的；有民主精神的；平等的

derivatives.zh: 民主；民主制度
民主主义者
以民主方式
使民主化
不民主的

senses.title: Run by the people
senses.definition: of a system in which people vote and share power
senses.definitionCN: 属于由人民投票并分享权力的制度的
senses.example: The country held its first democratic election in decades.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家举行了几十年来第一次民主选举。
senses.why: A system is democratic when power starts at the bottom and moves up.
senses.whyCN: 权力从下面长上去的制度，才叫民主的。

senses.title: Fair to every member
senses.definition: treating every member as having an equal say
senses.definitionCN: 让每个成员都拥有同等发言权的
senses.example: The club made a democratic decision to share the work equally.
senses.exampleCN: 这个社团以民主方式决定平分工作。
senses.why: The habit of voting can live in a small room as well as in a nation.
senses.whyCN: 投票的习惯既住在一个国家里，也住在一间小屋里。

intro.en: Democratic adds the Greek adjective ending -ic to democrat, which comes from demos, the people, and kratia, rule.
intro.cn: democratic 是 democrat 加上希腊形容词词尾 -ic；democrat 由 demos（人民）与 kratia（统治）组成。

items.en: Demokratia joined demos, the people, with kratia, rule.
items.cn: demokratia 由 demos（人民）与 kratia（统治）合成。

items.en: Athenian writers used demokratikos for things belonging to popular rule.
items.cn: 雅典作家用 demokratikos 形容属于民众统治的事物。

items.en: Latin authors borrowed the Greek adjective in discussions of constitutions.
items.cn: 拉丁作家在讨论政体时借用了这个希腊形容词。

items.en: English formed democratic to describe power held by the people.
items.cn: 英语造出 democratic，用来形容由人民掌握的权力。

items.en: Today it also describes any group that shares decisions fairly.
items.cn: 如今它也形容任何公平分享决定的群体。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the demo- opening, and the meaning group offers words for equal power and for standing in for others.
note.cn: 形近组都以 demo- 开头，近义组则给出表示平等权力与代表他人的词。

entries.definition: a person who believes in rule by the people
a system of government by the people
entries.definitionCN: 由人民治理的政治制度

entries.definition: the study of populations
chosen to speak for a group of people
entries.definitionCN: 被选出来代表一群人的

entries.definition: believing that all people should be equal
belonging to the ordinary people

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a circle of chairs and end with a decision that no single person could make alone.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一圈椅子开始，落到一个谁也独自做不出的决定。

normal.en: A circle of chairs has no head and no foot.
normal.cn: 围成一圈的椅子，没有头也没有尾。

normal.en: If one hand is always the only one raised, the room is not democratic.
normal.cn: 如果永远只有一只手举起，这间屋子就不民主。

normal.en: The word carries a Greek crowd inside it.
normal.cn: 这个词里装着一群希腊人。

normal.en: A vote in a classroom is small, but the habit is the same size as a nation.
normal.cn: 教室里的投票很小，习惯却和一个国家一样大。

normal.en: Demo- means people, so democratic means the people hold the pen.
normal.cn: demo- 是人民，democratic 就是人民握着笔。

abstract.en: Picture a hand count where every arm moves at the same time.
abstract.cn: 想象一次举手表决，所有手臂同时抬起。

abstract.en: Picture a rule book with one page that says no one is above it.
abstract.cn: 想象一本规则手册，其中一页写着没有人高过它。

abstract.en: Picture a small club where the leader also washes the cups.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小社团，负责人也要去洗杯子。

examples.en: The country held its first democratic election in decades.
examples.cn: 这个国家举行了几十年来第一次民主选举。

examples.en: The club made a democratic decision to share the work equally.
examples.cn: 这个社团以民主方式决定平分工作。

examples.en: A democratic classroom lets students disagree with the teacher.
examples.cn: 民主的课堂允许学生不同意老师。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 democratic 记成「得摸克拉提克」：demo 是人民，crat 是统治，ic 是形容词尾，人民统治的，就是民主的。

root: 来自希腊语 demokratikos，由 demos（人民）与 kratia（统治）再加形容词词尾 -ic 构成，经拉丁语与法语进入英语。它本指与人民统治有关的事物，后来也用来形容任何讲究平等参与的做法。

sensesIntro.en: From a nation that counts its votes, to a small room where every member counts once.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一个清点选票的国家，到一间每个成员都只算一票的小屋。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a circle of chairs where no seat is higher than another.
core.cn: 核心意象：一圈椅子，没有哪一张比别的更高。

branches.en: The first sense is a state whose power starts with votes.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是权力起始于选票的国家。

branches.en: The second sense is a room where every member counts once.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是每个成员都只算一票的屋子。

branches.en: A country and a club share the same test: who gets to speak.
branches.cn: 国家与社团面对同一道考题：谁有资格说话。

branches.en: The word also says who the power belongs to: the people, not a family.
branches.cn: 这个词也说明权力属于谁：属于人民，不属于某个家族。

branches.en: Used in small groups, it simply means no one sits above the vote.
branches.cn: 用在小组里，它只是说没有人坐在投票之上。

intro.en: Democratic grows a family of nouns and verbs about rule by the people and the act of opening a group to all.
intro.cn: democratic 长出一族名词与动词，讲人民统治，也讲把一个群体向所有人打开。

latinIntro.en: The Greek base is demos, the people, joined to kratia, rule, and then to the Latin adjective ending -ic.
latinIntro.cn: 它的希腊词基是 demos（人民）与 kratia（统治），后面接上形容词词尾 -ic。

items.meaning: based on equal power for all

items.exampleCN: 民主制度需要耐心的公民。

items.meaning: a believer in rule by the people
items.exampleCN: 他一生都是民主主义者。

items.meaning: in a fair and equal way
items.exampleCN: 领导者是以民主方式选出的。

items.meaning: to make something open to all
items.exampleCN: 他们把社团规则民主化了。

items.example: They voted for a social democratic party.
items.exampleCN: 他们投票给社会民主党。

definition_zh: 邪恶的；罪恶；祸害
definition_en: morally bad or harmful
core_image: 阴影里伸出的手，抓住一束光
scene: 故事里的巫师用邪恶的咒语夺走了村庄的光。 The wizard in the story used an evil spell to take away the light of the village.
sceneCN: 这里 evil 是「邪恶的」（第 1 个义项：道德上错误且残忍）；句意：故事里的巫师用邪恶的咒语夺走了村庄的光。

derivatives.zh: 邪恶地
邪恶
作恶者

senses.title: Morally bad
senses.definition: morally wrong and cruel
senses.definitionCN: 道德上错误且残忍
senses.example: The evil king was feared by all.
senses.exampleCN: 所有人都惧怕那个邪恶的国王。
senses.why: The oldest sense is what harms others by choice.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的含义是故意伤害他人。

senses.title: A great wrong
senses.definition: a very bad act or force
senses.definitionCN: 极坏的行为或力量
senses.example: They fought against evil in the world.
senses.exampleCN: 他们与世间的罪恶作斗争。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a noun for the force itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词变成指这种力量的名词。

senses.title: A harmful thing
senses.definition: something that causes great harm
senses.definitionCN: 造成巨大伤害的事物
senses.example: Greed is an evil that spreads quietly.
senses.exampleCN: 贪婪是一种悄然蔓延的祸害。
senses.why: Any great harm can be named an evil.
senses.whyCN: 任何巨大危害都可称为祸害。

intro.en: Evil is an old English word, yfel, shared by Germanic languages.
intro.cn: evil 是古英语词 yfel，在日耳曼语族中通用。

items.en: Yfel means bad or harmful.
items.cn: yfel 意为坏的或有害的。

items.en: The word is common to Germanic languages.
items.cn: 这个词在日耳曼语族中普遍存在。

items.en: Evil keeps the sense of moral harm.
items.cn: evil 保留了道德伤害的含义。

items.en: It also names the force of wrong.
items.cn: 它也指恶的力量。

items.en: Any great harm can be called an evil.
items.cn: 任何巨大危害都能称为祸害。

note.en: Evil implies deep moral wrong; bad is the general opposite of good.
note.cn: evil 指深刻的道德错误；bad 是 good 的通用反义词。

entries.definition: in an evil way
the quality of being evil
a person who does evil
morally very bad
causing pain on purpose
causing damage or injury

normalIntro.en: Evil is a shadow that chooses to swallow light.
normalIntro.cn: evil 是选择吞掉光明的阴影。

normal.en: An evil plan intends to hurt others.
normal.cn: an evil plan 意图伤害他人。

normal.en: Good and evil are old opposites.
normal.cn: good and evil 是古老的对照。

normal.en: An evil spirit is a harmful force.
normal.cn: an evil spirit 是害人的力量。

normal.en: The root of evil means the source of wrong.
normal.cn: the root of evil 意为罪恶的根源。

normal.en: Compare wicked: wicked stresses cruelty, evil stresses deep wrong.
normal.cn: 对比 wicked：wicked 强调残忍，evil 强调深刻的错误。

abstract.en: Picture a hand of shadow reaching through a beam of light.
abstract.cn: 想象一只影子般的手穿过一束光。

abstract.en: Imagine a sweet voice that hides a sharp edge.
abstract.cn: 想象一个甜美却暗藏锋刃的声音。

abstract.en: Think of a door that opens into a very cold room.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇通向极冷房间的门。

examples.en: The story is about the battle between good and evil.
examples.cn: 这个故事讲的是善与恶的斗争。

examples.en: He had an evil plan.
examples.cn: 他有一个邪恶的计划。

examples.en: The medicine left an evil taste.
examples.cn: 这药留下了一股难闻的味道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「evil」倒过来是「live」——把生活颠倒，就成了 evil；这只是字母游戏，非词源。

root: 古英语 yfel（坏的）→ 中古英语 evel → evil，核心义「故意为害的」。

sensesIntro.en: Evil begins as moral badness, becomes the force of wrong, and then any great harm.
sensesIntro.cn: evil 从道德败坏开始，变成恶的力量，再指任何巨大危害。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand of shadow reaching through a beam of light.
core.cn: 核心意象：影子般的手穿过一束光。

branches.en: Moral badness is the core sense.
branches.cn: 道德败坏是核心含义。

branches.en: The force of wrong becomes a noun.
branches.cn: 恶的力量成为名词。

branches.en: Any great harm can be an evil.
branches.cn: 任何巨大危害都可是祸害。

branches.en: A bad act and a bad force share one word.
branches.cn: 恶行与恶的力量共用一个词。

branches.en: Cruelty and harm are both part of evil.
branches.cn: 残忍与伤害都属于恶。

intro.en: Evil is an old English word with a Germanic root.
intro.cn: evil 是带日耳曼词根的古英语词。

latinIntro.en: It has no Latin source.
latinIntro.cn: 它没有拉丁语来源。

items.example: Yfel is the oldest recorded form.
items.exampleCN: yfel 是现存最古老的形式。

definition_zh: 索引；指数；指标；食指
definition_en: an alphabetical list at the end of a book, or a number that shows a level or change
core_image: 一根食指，指着书后的字母表，告诉你从哪一页找起
scene: 查资料时，先翻书末的索引比一页页读快得多。 Look it up in the index at the back of the book.
sceneCN: 这里 index 是「索引」（第 1 个义项：书末按字母排列的条目表）；句意是到书后的索引里查一下。

pos.zh: 名词：索引；指数；指标；食指
动词：为……编索引；把……列为指标

derivatives.zh: 义为「指数化」，指工资等按指数调整
义为「与指数挂钩的、附有索引的」
义为「编索引的人」

senses.title: A list pointing to pages
senses.definition: an alphabetical list of names or subjects with the pages where they appear
senses.definitionCN: 按字母排列的名称或主题表，并注明出现页码
senses.example: Look it up in the index at the back of the book.
senses.exampleCN: 到书后的索引里查一下。
senses.why: Latin index meant the finger that points, and a list of pointers is the same gesture in print.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 index 意为「指点的食指」，而一串指路的条目正是同一手势印在纸上。

senses.title: A number showing a level
senses.definition: a number that measures changes in prices, wages or production compared with a base
senses.definitionCN: 与基期相比，衡量价格、工资或产量变化的数字
senses.example: The price index rose again last month.
senses.exampleCN: 上个月物价指数又上涨了。
senses.why: A single number points to the state of a larger system, so economics borrowed the pointer.
senses.whyCN: 一个数字指向更大系统的状况，经济学于是借用了这根指头。

senses.title: A sign of something else
senses.definition: something that shows the level or condition of another thing
senses.definitionCN: 能显示另一事物水平或状况的东西
senses.example: Handwriting is a poor index of character.
senses.exampleCN: 笔迹不是反映性格的好指标。
senses.why: Any sign can point the way the finger does, so the word widens to evidence.
senses.whyCN: 任何迹象都能像食指那样指点方向，于是词义扩展到「证据」。

senses.title: The finger that points
senses.definition: the finger next to the thumb, used for pointing
senses.definitionCN: 拇指旁用来指点的指头
senses.example: He cut his index finger on a page.
senses.exampleCN: 他的食指被书页划破了。
senses.why: The oldest sense survives in the fixed phrase index finger, a trace of the word's birth.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项保存在 index finger 这个固定搭配里，留下词诞生的痕迹。

senses.title: To make an index, as a verb
senses.definition: to prepare an index for a book or to record items in one
senses.definitionCN: 为书编索引，或把条目录入索引
senses.example: The archive has indexed every letter.
senses.exampleCN: 档案馆已为每封信编了索引。
senses.why: Once the noun exists, the verb simply says what one does with it.
senses.whyCN: 名词一旦存在，动词只需说明拿它做什么。

intro.en: Index is Latin for a pointer or forefinger, from indicare, to point out.
intro.cn: index 是拉丁语中「指点者、食指」一词，源自 indicare「指出」。

items.en: Index meant the finger that points and also a sign or informer.
items.cn: index 指指点的食指，也指标志或告发者。

items.en: A title in a book was called an index because it pointed to chapters.
items.cn: 书的标题被称为 index，因为它指向各章。

items.en: Printing gave index the modern sense of an alphabetical list of pages.
items.cn: 印刷术赋予 index 现代含义：按字母排列的页码表。

items.en: Politics borrowed it for the Index of banned books.
items.cn: 政治借它指代「禁书目录」（Index）。

items.en: Statistics gave it the sense of a measuring number.
items.cn: 统计学又给了它「衡量数字」的含义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the indic- root; the near-meaning group holds words for lists and measures.
note.cn: 形近组共用 indic- 词根；近义组收表示目录与度量的词。

entries.definition: To show or point out something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「表明、指示」，同根。

entries.definition: The classical plural of index.
To start a line further from the margin.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「缩进」，与 index 形近。

entries.definition: The list of chapters at the front of a book.
A sign that shows a level or change.
An ordered list of items for reference.

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the pointing finger, the split plural and the stock market index.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借指点的食指、双重复数与股市指数。

normal.en: The index finger and the book index are the same word: both point where to look.
normal.cn: index finger 与书里的索引是同一个词：两者都指向该看的地方。

normal.en: Two plurals exist: indexes for lists and indices in science, as Latin once had it.
normal.cn: 它有两个复数：目录用 indexes，科学用 indices，沿用拉丁旧形。

normal.en: The Shanghai Composite is an index because one number points at hundreds of shares.
normal.cn: 上证指数之所以叫 index，是因为一个数字指向成百上千只股票。

normal.en: Contents tells you what chapters there are; index tells you where a word hides.
normal.cn: contents 告诉你有哪些章，index 告诉你某个词藏在哪。

normal.en: A poor index of character: a sign points at something without being that thing.
normal.cn: a poor index of character：标志指向某物，却并不等于该物。

abstract.en: To index is to decide in advance which words will be findable later.
abstract.cn: 编索引就是预先决定日后哪些词能被找到。

abstract.en: An index is a map of a book, and every map lies about something.
abstract.cn: 索引是一本书的地图，而每张地图都在某处有所隐瞒。

abstract.en: A single number that stands for a whole system always hides the disagreements inside it.
abstract.cn: 用一个数字代表整个系统，必然隐藏了其中的分歧。

examples.en: The report includes an index of names.
examples.cn: 报告附有一份人名索引。

examples.en: The consumer price index fell slightly.
examples.cn: 消费物价指数略有下降。

examples.en: She pointed with her index finger at the map.
examples.cn: 她用食指点着地图。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「印得克斯」——印刷时把条目印得整齐，还得配上索引。

root: 拉丁语 index（指点者、食指），源自 indicare（指出，由 in- + dic-「说」构成）；同根词有 indicate、dictate、dictionary、contradict。

sensesIntro.en: Index starts as a pointing finger, turns into a printed list of pointers, then into a number that points at a system, then into any sign at all, and finally into the act of making such a list.
sensesIntro.cn: index 起于指点的食指，转为纸上的指路表，再转为指向系统的数字，继而泛指任何标志，最后成为「编索引」这个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a forefinger pointing at a lettered list behind the book.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根食指指着书后按字母排列的表。

branches.en: BOOK LINE: a list points to pages.
branches.cn: 书本线：一份表指向各页。

branches.en: NUMBER LINE: one figure points at an economy.
branches.cn: 数字线：一个数字指向整个经济。

branches.en: EVIDENCE LINE: any sign can point at a condition.
branches.cn: 证据线：任何迹象都能指向某种状况。

branches.en: BODY LINE: the pointing finger keeps the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 身体线：指点的食指保留着最古老的义项。

branches.en: ACTION LINE: to index is to build the pointing list.
branches.cn: 动作线：编索引就是造出那张指路的表。

intro.en: A Latin root for pointing and saying, with a noun ending meaning one who does.
intro.cn: 一个意为「指出、说出」的拉丁词根，加一个表示「做某事者」的名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin indicare, to point out, with -ex, produced index, one who points.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 indicare「指出」加 -ex，构成 index「指点者」。

items.example: the root of dictate and dictionary
items.exampleCN: dictate 与 dictionary 的词根

items.meaning: to say aloud for another to write

definition_zh: 锅炉；煮器；热水器
definition_en: a tank or device that heats water or makes steam, often for heating a building
core_image: 地下室里轰隆作响、烧着热水的大铁罐
scene: 冬天来临前，工人下到地下室检查那只轰隆作响的大铁罐。 The old boiler in the basement finally broke down last night.
sceneCN: 这里 boiler 是「锅炉」（第 1 个义项：烧水供热的设备）；句意是地下室里那台旧锅炉昨晚终于坏了。

pos.zh: 名词：烧水加热的装置，常指供暖锅炉

derivatives.zh: 基础动词，指把水等液体煮至沸腾
由 boil 加 -ing 构成，义为「沸腾的；极热的」
由 boil 加 -ed 构成，义为「煮熟的」

senses.title: A device that heats water
senses.definition: a closed tank that heats water or produces steam for heating or power
senses.definitionCN: 加热水或产生蒸汽、用于供暖或提供动力的密闭容器
senses.example: The old boiler in the basement finally broke down last night.
senses.exampleCN: 地下室里那台旧锅炉昨晚终于坏了。
senses.why: The -er suffix names a tool by the action it performs, so a boiler is the thing that boils.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -er 用动作来命名工具，boiler 就是「用来煮水的东西」。

senses.title: A vessel for boiling food or liquid
senses.definition: a pot or container used for boiling things, such as a fish kettle
senses.definitionCN: 用来煮东西的锅或容器，如煮鱼的长锅
senses.example: She put the ham into a large boiler and let it simmer for hours.
senses.exampleCN: 她把火腿放进一口大煮锅里，小火煨了好几个小时。
senses.why: The same tool-naming logic extends to everyday cookware that boils food.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「以动作命名工具」逻辑延伸到了日常煮食的锅具。

senses.title: A very hot room or situation
senses.definition: informally, a hot, stuffy place that feels like being boiled
senses.definitionCN: 非正式用法，指热得像被蒸煮一样的闷热地方
senses.example: Without air conditioning, the dorm turned into a boiler in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 没有空调，夏天宿舍闷热得像个蒸笼。
senses.why: The heat of a boiler becomes a vivid image for any stiflingly hot place.
senses.whyCN: 锅炉的高温被拿来比喻任何闷热难耐的场所。

intro.en: Boiler is a straightforward English formation: the verb boil plus the agent suffix -er.
intro.cn: boiler 是一个直白的英语构词：动词 boil 加上施动者后缀 -er。

items.en: boillir meant to bubble and seethe, a general thought to come from Latin bullire.
items.cn: boillir 意为冒泡翻滚，一般认为源自拉丁语 bullire（沸腾）。

items.en: bullire, from bulla a bubble, described liquid at a rolling boil.
items.cn: bullire 来自 bulla（气泡），描述液体剧烈沸腾。

items.en: boilen entered English by the thirteenth century with the meaning to seethe.
items.cn: 十三世纪前后 boilen 进入英语，意为翻滚沸腾。

items.en: boiler first named a pot for boiling, recorded in craft contexts.
items.cn: boiler 最早指煮东西的锅，见于手工业语境。

items.en: steam engines made the closed heating boiler central to industry.
items.cn: 蒸汽机时代，密闭的供热锅炉成为工业核心设备。

items.en: boiler now mainly means the heating unit in a home or factory.
items.cn: 如今 boiler 主要指家庭或工厂里的供热锅炉。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -er ending; the near-meaning group names heating devices.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -er 结尾；近义组是各类加热设备。

entries.definition: to heat a liquid until it bubbles
entries.definitionCN: 把液体加热至沸腾；boiler 的基础动词

entries.definition: a device that cooks food with strong direct heat
entries.definitionCN: 烤箱上部的炙烤装置；与 boiler 拼写相近但词根不同

entries.definition: a container or device that keeps things cold
entries.definitionCN: 冷藏箱或冷却装置；同为 -er 工具名词，词义与 boiler 相反

entries.definition: an enclosed chamber for very high heat
entries.definitionCN: furnace 指高炉、火炉，靠燃烧直接供热

entries.definition: any device that gives out heat
entries.definitionCN: 泛指各类取暖器；boiler 特指烧水锅炉

entries.definition: a device that sends heat into a room, often fed by a boiler
entries.definitionCN: 暖气片，常由锅炉供热的热水驱动

normalIntro.en: Build the word from its verb and suffix.
normalIntro.cn: 从动词加后缀来搭建这个词。

normal.en: boil + er = the thing that boils water.
normal.cn: boil（煮）+ er（工具）＝煮水的装置，即锅炉。

normal.en: A boiler makes the water boil for radiators.
normal.cn: 锅炉烧出热水，送进暖气片。

normal.en: boil, boiling, boiled, boiler all share the same family.
normal.cn: boil、boiling、boiled、boiler 属于同族词。

normal.en: The Latin bulla, a bubble, hides inside boil.
normal.cn: boil 里藏着拉丁词 bulla（气泡）。

normal.en: boiler room is where the big hot tank lives.
normal.cn: boiler room 就是锅炉房，大铁罐所在之处。

abstract.en: Picture a round iron belly bubbling with steam.
abstract.cn: 想象一只铁肚子在咕嘟咕嘟冒着蒸汽。

abstract.en: Hear the low hum of a working boiler in winter.
abstract.cn: 聆听冬天里锅炉运转的低鸣。

abstract.en: Feel the warm pipes leaving the boiler like veins.
abstract.cn: 感受从锅炉伸出的管道，像血管一样输送暖意。

examples.en: The old boiler in the basement finally broke down last night.
examples.cn: 地下室里那台旧锅炉昨晚终于坏了。

examples.en: They replaced the gas boiler before the cold season arrived.
examples.cn: 他们在寒冷季节到来前更换了燃气锅炉。

examples.en: Water boils at one hundred degrees at sea level.
examples.cn: 在海平面，水在一百度沸腾。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「抱勒儿」——锅炉抱住火焰，勒住热水不外泄，一只轰隆作响的大铁罐。

root: boiler 由英语动词 boil（沸腾）加名词后缀 -er 构成；boil 一般认为经由古法语 boillir 来自拉丁语 bullire（沸腾），bullire 又出自 bulla（气泡）。构词法与 worker、cooler 等工具名词一致。

sensesIntro.en: From a pot that boils, to the heating device of industry, to any stifling hot place.
sensesIntro.cn: 从煮食的锅，到工业供热锅炉，再到闷热难耐之处，词义围绕「煮」的核心意象展开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tank that boils water
core.cn: 核心意象：一口烧水的罐子

branches.en: Cookware that boils food
branches.cn: 煮食的锅具，词义的最初形态

branches.en: The closed water-heating tank of homes
branches.cn: 家庭供热锅炉，现代主要义项

branches.en: Heat radiating outward from the device
branches.cn: 设备向外散发的热，引出闷热比喻

branches.en: A hot, stuffy room feels like a boiler
branches.cn: 闷热难耐之处，意象化引申

branches.en: Steam boilers powering industry
branches.cn: 工业蒸汽锅炉，动力来源

intro.en: Boiler shows the classic agent-suffix pattern of English tools.
intro.cn: boiler 体现了英语典型的「动词 + -er 命名工具」构词模式。

latinIntro.en: The verb boils back to Latin bullire, from bulla a bubble.
latinIntro.cn: 动词 boil 一般认为可回溯到拉丁语 bullire（沸腾），其词根是 bulla（气泡）。

items.meaning: one that does or a device that does
items.meaningCN: 施动者；执行动作的工具
items.exampleCN: 锅炉、冷藏器、取暖器都由动词加 -er 命名

items.example: Latin bullire gave Old French boillir
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 bullire 演变为古法语 boillir

items.example: bulla is the root idea behind bullire
items.exampleCN: bulla 是 bullire 的词根意象

items.meaningCN: 炙烤器；与 boiler 拼写相近但词根不同

沸腾的；极热的

definition_zh: 旋转；纺纱；眩晕；疾驰；杜撰（故事）；（名）旋转；兜风
definition_en: to turn round and round quickly, or to twist fibres into thread
core_image: 指尖一捻，陀螺在桌上转出一片模糊的圆
scene: 教室的桌上，一只彩漆陀螺正转得发亮。 The girl watched the top spin until it wobbled and fell.
sceneCN: 这里 spin 是「旋转」（第 1 个义项：快速绕轴转动）；句意为女孩看着陀螺旋转，直到它摇晃倒下。图中可辨识物件：陀螺、课桌、铅笔盒。

pos.zh: 动词：旋转；纺纱；疾驰；杜撰
名词：旋转；兜风；杜撰的报道

derivatives.zh: 由动词加施动后缀构成，义为「纺纱工；旋转器」
由动词加名词化后缀构成，义为「纺纱；旋转运动」
由动词加副词构成，义为「派生产品；副产品」
由纺纱义加施动后缀构成，义为「未婚女子（旧用法）」

senses.title: To turn round and round
senses.definition: to turn quickly around a central point or axis
senses.definitionCN: 围绕中心点或轴快速转动
senses.example: The fans spun above the hot courtroom.
senses.exampleCN: 风扇在闷热的法庭上方旋转。
senses.why: One point holds still while the rest sweeps circles around it.
senses.whyCN: 一点静止，其余围绕它画圆。

senses.title: To twist fibres into thread
senses.definition: to draw out and twist fibres such as wool into thread
senses.definitionCN: 把羊毛等纤维拉出并捻成线
senses.example: Her grandmother could spin wool into fine thread.
senses.exampleCN: 她祖母能把羊毛纺成细线。
senses.why: The same circling motion twists loose fibres into one held line.
senses.whyCN: 同样的旋转动作把松散纤维捻成一条被握住的线。

senses.title: To seem to whirl before the eyes
senses.definition: to seem to whirl, as when a person feels dizzy
senses.definitionCN: 似在旋转，如人感到头晕时
senses.example: The room began to spin after the fairground ride.
senses.exampleCN: 玩过游乐设施后，房间开始天旋地转。
senses.why: The world itself seems to take up the spinning.
senses.whyCN: 世界仿佛自己也转了起来。

senses.title: To move swiftly in a vehicle
senses.definition: to ride or drive swiftly, often for pleasure
senses.definitionCN: 乘车疾驰，常为消遣
senses.example: They took the old car out for a spin along the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 他们开着旧车沿海岸兜风。
senses.why: Wheels spinning carry the rider out of the ordinary road.
senses.whyCN: 旋转的车轮把乘坐者带出日常之路。

senses.title: To present facts favourably
senses.definition: to present information in a way that favours one side
senses.definitionCN: 以偏向一方的方式呈现信息
senses.example: The office spun the poor figures as steady progress.
senses.exampleCN: 办公室把糟糕的数据粉饰成稳步推进。
senses.why: The twisting motion turns plain facts into a shaped line, like fibre into thread.
senses.whyCN: 扭转的动作把平实事实捻成有形状的线，如纤维成线。

senses.title: To invent or tell a story
senses.definition: to tell or invent a story, as in spin a yarn
senses.definitionCN: 讲述或编造故事，如 spin a yarn
senses.example: The old sailor spun a yarn about a sea serpent.
senses.exampleCN: 老水手编了个海蛇的故事。
senses.why: Storytelling and threading share the same word: a tale is spun from loose talk.
senses.whyCN: 讲故事与纺线共用一词：故事由散漫话语捻成。

senses.title: A rapid turning movement
senses.definition: a quick turning movement around a central axis
senses.definitionCN: 围绕中轴的快速转动
senses.example: The skater finished with a graceful spin.
senses.exampleCN: 滑冰者以一个优雅的旋转收尾。
senses.why: The verb freezes into a noun: the circle itself is named.
senses.whyCN: 动词凝为名词：圆周本身被指名。

senses.title: A derivative product or company
senses.definition: a new product or company developed from an existing one, as in spin-off
senses.definitionCN: 由既有产品或公司派生的新产品或新公司，如 spin-off
senses.example: The research lab produced several useful spin-offs.
senses.exampleCN: 该研究实验室产出了几个有用的副产品。
senses.why: The thread spun from the main yarn becomes its own cloth.
senses.whyCN: 从主线捻出的线自成一块布。

intro.en: Spin is a native English word of the thread and wheel world, rooted in the old craft of twisting fibre.
intro.cn: spin 是本土英语词，属于线与轮的世界，根植于捻纤维的古老手艺。

items.en: *spinnan- is generally reconstructed as "to draw out and twist thread"; the deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始日耳曼语 *spinnan- 表示「拉出并捻线」；更早来源不确定。

items.en: Old English spinnan meant "to spin thread", the everyday work of households.
items.cn: 古英语 spinnan 意为「纺线」，是家家户户的日常劳作。

items.en: The agent noun spinne gave English spinster, once simply a woman who spun.
items.cn: 施动名词 spinne 给出英语 spinster，本义仅为纺纱女子。

items.en: The sense widened to whirling motion, dizziness, and swift riding.
items.cn: 中古英语时期，词义扩展到旋转、眩晕与疾驰。

items.en: Politics added the sense of favourable presentation, and business the spin-off.
items.cn: 政治领域加上了粉饰义，商业领域则产生了 spin-off。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the native twisting family and near spellings; the near-meaning group gathers words for turning and twisting.
note.cn: 形近组收本土「捻线」词族与拼写相近的词；近义组收表示转动与扭转的词。

entries.definition: One who spins thread, or a device that spins.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指纺纱工或旋转装置。

entries.definition: Once a woman who spun wool; now an unmarried woman in older usage.
entries.definitionCN: 原指纺纱女子，旧用法中指未婚女子。

entries.definition: A product or company derived from an existing one.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指由既有事物派生的产品或公司。

entries.definition: The past tense and participle of spin.
The backbone of a body or book; merely looks similar and is of different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「脊柱、书脊」；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To turn around an axis, often regular and measured.
entries.definitionCN: 绕轴转动，常有规律、可测量。

entries.definition: To orbit or turn around a centre.
To wind threads or parts together; overlaps the fibre sense.
entries.definitionCN: 把线或部件缠在一起，与纤维义项重叠。

entries.definition: To turn rapidly and confusedly; overlaps the dizzy sense.
entries.definitionCN: 急速而纷乱地转，与眩晕义项重叠。

entries.definition: To move or turn as if on wheels.

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real spinning craft and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的纺纱手艺，以及该词常出现的搭配。

normal.en: Spin a yarn is the idiom that keeps the old thread craft.
normal.cn: spin a yarn 是保留古老纺线手艺的习语。

normal.en: The past form is spun: the wheel spun all night.
normal.cn: 过去式是 spun：车轮转了一整夜。

normal.en: Spinster began as simply a woman who spun.
normal.cn: spinster 起初仅指纺纱的女子。

normal.en: Go for a spin means a short fast drive.
normal.cn: go for a spin 指一次短途疾驰。

normal.en: A spin-off is thread twisted off the main yarn.
normal.cn: spin-off 是从主线捻出的线。

abstract.en: Picture a fingertip on a coin: one held point, everything else circling.
abstract.cn: 想象指尖按住一枚硬币：一点被按住，其余画圆。

abstract.en: A story is wool in the hand: loose until spun into a line.
abstract.cn: 故事如掌中羊毛：捻成线之前是散的。

abstract.en: When the room spins, the axis has slipped out of your ear.
abstract.cn: 房间旋转时，轴线从你的耳中滑脱了。

examples.en: The wheels of the cart spun wildly in the mud.
examples.cn: 车轮在泥中疯狂空转。

examples.en: She spun the wool into a strong warm thread.
examples.cn: 她把羊毛纺成结实保暖的线。

examples.en: The agency spun the data to protect its budget.
examples.cn: 该机构粉饰数据以保住预算。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯宾」——指尖捻动转出圆，羊毛捻成线：旋转；纺纱

root: spin 属日耳曼语本土词：古英语 spinnan「纺线」，一般认为源于原始日耳曼语 *spinnan-「拉出并捻线」，更早来源不确定；旋转、眩晕与疾驰诸义均为纺纱这一旋转动作的延伸。

sensesIntro.en: The senses of spin all turn one axis: wheels, threads, dizzy rooms, fast cars, shaped stories and new companies.
sensesIntro.cn: spin 的各项义项都绕同一根轴转：车轮、线、眩晕的房间、疾驰的车、成形的故事与新公司。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a held centre with everything else sweeping circles around it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一点被握住，其余围绕它画圆。

branches.en: THE MOTION LINE: wheels, dizzy rooms and skater turns share one circling centre.
branches.cn: 运动线：车轮、眩晕的房间与滑冰转体共享同一圆心。

branches.en: THE THREAD LINE: fibre, tales and facts are twisted into one held line.
branches.cn: 纺线线：纤维、故事与事实被捻成一条被握住的线。

branches.en: THE ROAD LINE: spinning wheels carry riders swiftly out of the ordinary.
branches.cn: 道路线：旋转的车轮载着乘坐者疾速脱离日常。

branches.en: THE PRESENTATION LINE: facts are shaped like fibre to favour one side.
branches.cn: 陈述线：事实像纤维一样被捻向有利一方。

branches.en: THE OFFSHOOT LINE: thread spun off the main yarn becomes its own cloth.
branches.cn: 派生线：从主线捻出的线自成一块布。

intro.en: Spin is a bare native root; compounds and agent nouns gather around it.
intro.cn: spin 是本土裸词根；复合词与施动名词围绕它聚集。

latinIntro.en: Spin is Germanic in origin, so its Latin cognates list is empty; the Germanic root is a reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: spin 属日耳曼语源，因此拉丁同源词列表为空；日耳曼词根为重构形式。

items.example: The old verb is the direct source.
The vowel change marks the old strong verb.
items.exampleCN: 元音变化标出古老强变化动词。

items.example: The idiom joins the two main senses.
items.exampleCN: 该习语连接两个主要义项。

items.example: It completes the phrase spin out.
The Old English verb is the direct source.

derivatives.zh: 由动词加施动后缀构成，义为「纺纱工；旋转器」
由动词加名词化后缀构成，义为「纺纱；旋转运动」
由动词加副词构成，义为「派生产品；副产品」
由纺纱义加施动后缀构成，义为「未婚女子（旧用法）」

definition_zh: 回答；回应；作出反应
definition_en: to answer, or to react to something
core_image: 有人敲门，屋里的人立刻应声
scene: 老师提问后，她立刻举手回答。 When the teacher asked, she raised her hand and responded at once.
sceneCN: 这里 responded 是 respond 的过去式，表示「回答」（第 1 个义项：用语言回应）；句意：老师提问后，她立刻举手回答。

derivatives.zh: 回答；反应
回答者；受访者
反应迅速的；回应积极的

senses.title: To answer in words
senses.definition: to say or write something in reply
senses.definitionCN: 用口头或书面方式作出答复
senses.example: She responded to the question with a smile.
senses.exampleCN: 她微笑着回答了这个问题。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to promise in return, so answering is a return of words.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「回以承诺」，因此回答就是言语上的回赠。

senses.title: To react to something
senses.definition: to act or change as a result of something
senses.definitionCN: 因某事物而行动或发生变化
senses.example: The patient responded well to the treatment.
senses.exampleCN: 病人对治疗反应良好。
senses.why: A reply can be an action as well as a sentence, so the word covers reactions.
senses.whyCN: 回应既可以是行动也可以是话语，因此这个词涵盖各种反应。

senses.title: To act on a need or appeal
senses.definition: to take action in answer to a request, emergency, or need
senses.definitionCN: 针对请求、紧急情况或需求采取行动
senses.example: Firefighters responded within minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 消防员几分钟内就赶到了。
senses.why: A formal reply to an appeal is carried out as an action.
senses.whyCN: 对呼吁的正式回应会落实为行动。

intro.en: Respond comes from Latin respondere, to promise in return, from re-, back, and spondere, to promise.
intro.cn: respond 来自拉丁语 respondere（回以承诺），由 re-（回）与 spondere（承诺）构成。

items.en: Spondere means to promise solemnly.
items.cn: spondere 意为郑重承诺。

items.en: Respondere means to promise or answer in return.
items.cn: respondere 意为回以承诺或答复。

items.en: Responsum is the noun for an answer.
items.cn: responsum 是表示回答的名词。

items.en: Respondre carries the answering sense.
items.cn: respondre 保留「回答」的含义。

items.en: Respond means to answer or react.
items.cn: 中古英语 respond 意为回答或反应。

items.en: Modern English extends respond to medical and emergency reactions.
items.cn: 现代英语把 respond 扩展到医疗与紧急反应。

note.en: Respond is the verb of the response family, close to answer and react words.
note.cn: respond 是 response 词族的动词，与表示回答和反应的词相邻。

entries.definition: an answer or reaction
a person who answers
reacting quickly
to reply to a question
to say something back
to act in response

normalIntro.en: Respond is a return word: something comes to you, and you send an answer back.
normalIntro.cn: respond 是「回赠」词：有东西来到你面前，你把回应送回去。

normal.en: Respond to a question means answer it.
normal.cn: respond to a question 就是回答问题。

normal.en: Patients may respond well to a new drug.
normal.cn: 病人可能对新药反应良好。

normal.en: Emergency teams respond to calls for help.
normal.cn: 应急队伍响应求助呼叫。

normal.en: The noun response names the answer or reaction.
normal.cn: 名词 response 指回答或反应。

normal.en: Compare reply: reply is mostly verbal, respond also covers actions.
normal.cn: 对比 reply：reply 多为口头，respond 也涵盖行动。

abstract.en: Picture a knock at the door and a voice calling back.
abstract.cn: 想象有人敲门，屋里传出应答声。

abstract.en: Imagine a plant turning its leaves toward the sun.
abstract.cn: 想象植物把叶片转向太阳。

abstract.en: Think of a hand raised the moment a question is asked.
abstract.cn: 想象问题刚提出就有一只手举起。

examples.en: He did not respond to my email.
examples.cn: 他没有回复我的邮件。

examples.en: The engine responds quickly to the pedal.
examples.cn: 发动机对油门反应迅速。

examples.en: Volunteers responded to the call for help.
examples.cn: 志愿者们响应了求助号召。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re + spond」——把话「回」过去，就是回答；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（回）＋ spondere（承诺）→ respondere（回以承诺、答复）→ 英语 respond，核心义「把回应送回原处」。

sensesIntro.en: Respond starts as a verbal answer, then becomes any reaction, and finally action taken in answer to a need.
sensesIntro.cn: respond 从口头答复开始，随后指任何反应，最后指针对需求采取的行动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an answer sent back to the one who called.
core.cn: 核心意象：把答复送回给发问的人。

branches.en: A verbal answer is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 口头答复是基本义项。

branches.en: Any reaction extends the answer beyond words.
branches.cn: 任何反应都让答复超越语言。

branches.en: Answering an appeal becomes action.
branches.cn: 回应呼吁落实为行动。

branches.en: A patient and a student both give back a result.
branches.cn: 病人与学生都会给出一个回馈结果。

branches.en: Reacting quickly is the first step in helping.
branches.cn: 迅速反应是提供帮助的第一步。

intro.en: Respond is a Latin promising verb, and English builds response, respondent, and responsive on it.
intro.cn: respond 是拉丁语中表示承诺的动词，英语由它构成 response、respondent 与 responsive。

latinIntro.en: Latin spondere means to promise, and respondere means to promise or answer in return.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 spondere 意为承诺，respondere 意为回以承诺或答复。

definition_zh: 改进；改善；改进之处
definition_en: the act of making something better, or a change that makes something better than before
core_image: 同一段路前后对比：左边坑坑洼洼，右边新铺的柏油在阳光下泛光
scene: 村口那条土路修好之后，孩子们推着车跑得飞快，不再怕下雨天。 Someone said the road had seen no improvement in twenty years.
sceneCN: 这里 improvement 是「改进、改善」（第 1 个义项：让情况变好的改变），句意是新排水系统是这些年来学校最大的一处改变。画面里有修好的村路、推车跑过的小孩和新铺的柏油。

pos.zh: 名词：改进、改善；改进之处；进步

derivatives.zh: 改进、好转
有启发的、使人进步的
改进者；改良剂

senses.title: The act of making better
senses.definition: the process of making something better in quality or condition
senses.definitionCN: 使事物在质量或状况上变好的过程
senses.example: The improvement of the water supply took two years.
senses.exampleCN: 供水系统的改善花了两年时间。
senses.why: The -ment suffix names the action itself, so this sense is about the work rather than the result.
senses.whyCN: -ment 后缀指的是动作本身，所以这一义项说的是功夫，而不是结果。

senses.title: A change that makes things better
senses.definition: one particular change that makes a place, plan, or product better
senses.definitionCN: 某一处让地方、计划或产品变得更好的具体改动
senses.example: A second window was the only improvement the room needed.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间唯一需要改的就是再加一扇窗。
senses.why: From the process the noun turns countable and points to a single piece of work done.
senses.whyCN: 名词从过程变为可数，指向具体做成的某一处。

senses.title: Getting better in health or skill
senses.definition: the way a person's condition or ability gets better over time
senses.definitionCN: 一个人的状况或能力随时间变好的过程
senses.example: The doctor saw a slow improvement in his breathing.
senses.exampleCN: 医生看到他的呼吸在慢慢好转。
senses.why: The subject here is a person, so improvement describes recovery or growth rather than repair.
senses.whyCN: 这里的主语是人，所以 improvement 指的是康复或长进，而非修补。

intro.en: Improvement comes from the same French root as improve, which once meant turning something to profit.
intro.cn: improvement 与 improve 同源，都出自法语，原意是「使之有利可图」。

items.en: En prou meant into profit, and the verb emprouwer meant to make land yield more.
items.cn: 古法语 en prou 意为「进入收益」，动词 emprouwer 意为让土地多出产。

items.en: The noun formed on the same stem with the -ment ending that marks a result.
items.cn: 名词由同一词干加表示结果的 -ment 词尾构成。

items.en: English took it as improvement, first used for the work known as land improvement.
items.cn: 英语借入后写作 improvement，最初指今天仍称「土地改良」的那种活。

items.en: As the verb widened, the noun followed, covering buildings, methods, skills, and health.
items.cn: 随着动词义扩展，名词也跟着扩展，涵盖房屋、方法、技能与健康。

items.en: The plural improvements became the usual way to speak of separate works done to a place.
items.cn: 复数 improvements 成了指同一处地方所做的几项不同工程时的常用说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the improve family and its false friends; the near-meaning group gathers other nouns of progress.
note.cn: 形近组收 improve 一族词及易混词；近义组收其他表示「进步」的名词。

entries.definition: The verb that carries out the change.
entries.definitionCN: 动词形式，负责做出改变。

entries.definition: The same -ment ending on a different verb, meaning a shift of position.
entries.definitionCN: 同一 -ment 词尾接在另一个动词上，意为「移动」。

entries.definition: Official consent, from approve, which differs from improve by one letter.
entries.definitionCN: 「批准」，出自 approve，与 improve 只差一个字母。

entries.definition: Forward movement toward a goal over time.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「进展」，指朝着目标向前推进。

entries.definition: A change to a better model or a higher class.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「升级」，换成更好的型号或更高档次。

entries.definition: A planned change to a system that is thought to be faulty.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「改革」，针对被认为有缺陷的制度所做的改变。

normalIntro.en: The hooks work on the -ment result ending and on the fixed phrases that treat improvement as a countable gain.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子围绕表示结果的 -ment 词尾，以及把改进当成「可数收获」的固定搭配。

normal.en: Add -ment to improve and you get the thing done, just as a payment is the thing paid.
normal.cn: improve 加 -ment 得到「做成的结果」，就像 payment 是付出去的那笔钱。

normal.en: Room for improvement is the polite phrase for work still undone.
normal.cn: room for improvement 是委婉地说「还有活没干」。

normal.en: Make improvements to a place means leave it better than you found it.
normal.cn: make improvements to 一个地方，就是把那里弄得比来时更好。

normal.en: In medicine and sport, improvement is usually uncountable: a slow improvement, not an improvement of two.
normal.cn: 在医学和运动语境里，improvement 通常不可数，只说「慢慢好转」。

normal.en: Do not mix it with approval; one letter changes a better road into a signed form.
normal.cn: 别和 approval 搞混，差一个字母，路变好了就成了签字盖章。

abstract.en: The word once meant profit from land, and it still measures gain against what a place used to yield.
abstract.cn: 这个词原指从土地获利，如今仍在用「从前出产多少」来衡量增益。

abstract.en: Countable improvements are promises kept one by one, and they are what voters and patients actually feel.
abstract.cn: 可数的改进是一条条兑现的承诺，也是选民和病患真正感受到的东西。

abstract.en: Because it compares with the past, improvement can never be declared in the present tense alone.
abstract.cn: 因为它是和过去相比，所以改进不能只靠现在时来宣布。

examples.en: There has been a clear improvement in air quality this winter.
examples.cn: 今年冬天的空气质量有了明显改善。

examples.en: The essay is good but there is room for improvement in the last paragraph.
examples.cn: 这篇文章不错，不过最后一段还有改进余地。

examples.en: Watering the garden was the only improvement the new tenant asked for.
examples.cn: 给花园装浇水设备是新房客唯一提出的改进。

dict_mnemonic.text: improve 改进 + -ment 名词词尾——改进这件事或改进之处

root: 与 improve 同源，出自共同源于古法语的构词（en prou「进入收益」），名词形式先在英语中出现（improvement），最初指对土地与庄园所做的改良，后泛指建筑、方法、技能与健康方面的改善。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: the work of making better, one particular better change, and a person's recovery or growth.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：改进这件事，某一处具体的改动，以及人在健康或技能上的好转。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two versions of the same road, one rutted and one freshly paved.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一条路的前后两版，一版坑洼，一版刚铺好柏油。

branches.en: THE WORK: improvement names the work done, often uncountable.
branches.cn: 工夫线：improvement 指所做的工夫，常为不可数。

branches.en: THE ITEM: made countable, it is one finished better thing.
branches.cn: 条目线：变成可数时，就是一处做好的改动。

branches.en: THE PERSON: for people it means recovery and growth.
branches.cn: 人身线：用在人身上，指康复与长进。

branches.en: THE PHRASE: room for improvement softens criticism.
branches.cn: 搭配线：room for improvement 把批评说软了。

branches.en: THE FARM: the land origin still shows in phrase like land improvement.
branches.cn: 农事线：改良土地这类说法里仍看得见它的出身。

intro.en: The table compares -ment nouns of result with the verbs that produce them.
intro.cn: 此表把表示结果的 -ment 名词与其来源动词放在一起比较。

latinIntro.en: The verb is Old French rather than Latin, though -ment itself came from Latin -mentum.
latinIntro.cn: 这个动词来自古法语而非拉丁语，但 -ment 本身出自拉丁语 -mentum。

items.meaning: the act or the better thing
items.example: The new lights are a small improvement.
A sudden movement scared the bird.
items.exampleCN: 一个突然的动作吓到了那只鸟。

items.meaningCN: 名词：成就，同一 -ment 模式
items.example: Finishing the course was a real achievement.
items.exampleCN: 读完这门课确实是件成就。

items.meaningCN: 名词：协议，同一 -ment 模式
items.example: They reached agreement in an hour.
items.exampleCN: 他们一小时内达成了协议。

items.example: The lessons had an improving effect.
items.exampleCN: 这些课有使人进步的作用。

items.meaning: one who or that which improves
items.example: Soil improver is added before planting.
items.exampleCN: 种植前会加土壤改良剂。

items.example: The unimproved lane is still muddy.
items.exampleCN: 那条没修过的小路还很泥泞。

latinEntries.meaning: a suffix naming the result of an action
latinEntries.meaningCN: 拉丁语后缀：表示动作的结果

latinEntries.meaning: to make better, the Latin cousin of the idea
latinEntries.meaningCN: 拉丁语动词：使变好，表示同一概念的拉丁表亲

definition_zh: 便利的；手边的；手巧的
definition_en: useful and easy to use, kept near at hand, or good at using your hands
core_image: 工具箱放在伸手可及的地方
scene: 这把小刀很方便携带。 This small knife is handy to carry.
sceneCN: 这里 handy 是「便利的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这把小刀很方便携带。

derivatives.zh: 方便地；轻松地
便利；灵巧

senses.title: Easy to use
senses.definition: useful and easy to use
senses.definitionCN: 有用且容易使用
senses.example: This small knife is handy to carry.
senses.exampleCN: 这把小刀很方便携带。
senses.why: Usefulness with ease is the central sense.
senses.whyCN: 好用又省力，是中心义项。

senses.title: Near at hand
senses.definition: kept near and ready to be used
senses.definitionCN: 放在近处、随时可用
senses.example: Keep the torch handy in case of a power cut.
senses.exampleCN: 把手电放在手边，以防停电。
senses.why: Nearness to the hand is part of being handy.
senses.whyCN: 在手边，是 handy 含义的一部分。

senses.title: Skilled with hands

definition_zh: 建筑师；缔造者；设计者；架构师
definition_en: a person who designs buildings, or someone who creates and guides a large plan, idea, or system
core_image: 在蓝图上勾出一条屋脊线，让想法有了骨架
scene: 绘图桌前，一支铅笔在蓝图上勾出屋脊线。 The architect sketched the outline of the museum on tracing paper.
sceneCN: 这里 architect 是「建筑师」（第 1 个义项：设计建筑的人）；句意为「建筑师在描图纸上勾出博物馆的轮廓」。画面里有绘图桌、蓝图与描图纸上的轮廓线。

pos.zh: 名词：建筑师；缔造者；设计者；架构师

derivatives.zh: 由本词换后缀构成，义为「建筑学；建筑风格；体系结构」

senses.title: A designer of buildings
senses.definition: a person trained to design buildings and supervise their construction
senses.definitionCN: 受过训练、负责设计建筑并监督施工的人
senses.example: The architect sketched the outline of the museum on tracing paper.
senses.exampleCN: 建筑师在描图纸上勾出博物馆的轮廓。
senses.why: Greek arkhitekton joined 'chief' and 'builder': the architect is the one who directs the building.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 arkhitekton 把「首要的」与「建造者」连在一起：建筑师就是指挥建造的人。

senses.title: The creator of a large undertaking
senses.definition: a person who plans and guides a large undertaking, such as a reform or an institution
senses.definitionCN: 筹划并引导一项大型事业的人，如改革或机构
senses.example: He was the architect of the peace agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 他是这份和平协议的缔造者。
senses.why: The image of a building spreads to any large structure: a treaty also needs a plan and a builder.
senses.whyCN: 建筑的意象扩散到任何大型结构：一份条约同样需要图纸与建造者。

senses.title: A designer of systems
senses.definition: a person who designs the structure of a computer system or a large organization
senses.definitionCN: 设计计算机系统或大型组织整体结构的人
senses.example: She works as a systems architect for the bank.
senses.exampleCN: 她在银行担任系统架构师。
senses.why: A system has parts that must bear weight and fit together, just as a building does.
senses.whyCN: 系统也有必须承重并彼此吻合的部件，正如一栋建筑。

senses.title: The first planner of an idea
senses.definition: the original creator of a method, idea, or style
senses.definitionCN: 某种方法、思想或风格的最初创造者
senses.example: He is remembered as the architect of modern ecology.
senses.exampleCN: 他被人们记作现代生态学的开创者。
senses.why: Whoever draws the first plan of a new field is its architect.
senses.whyCN: 谁为一个新领域画出第一张图，谁就是它的缔造者。

intro.en: Architect is a Greek word carried into English through Latin and French, and it still means chief builder.
intro.cn: architect 是一个经拉丁语与法语传入英语的希腊词，意思仍是「首要的建造者」。

items.en: Tekton means 'builder, craftsman', the everyday word for a worker in wood or stone.
items.cn: tekton 意为「建造者、匠人」，是木石工匠的日常称呼。

items.en: Arkhi- 'chief' plus tekton gave arkhitekton, 'chief builder, master builder'.
items.cn: arkhi-「首要的」与 tekton 构成 arkhitekton，意为「总建造师、匠师」。

items.en: Latin borrows the Greek word as architectus, keeping the sense of a master designer.
items.cn: 拉丁语把希腊词借作 architectus，保留「设计主事者」的意思。

items.en: French architecte passes the word into English in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 法语 architecte 在十六世纪把这个词送入英语。

items.en: The word extends from buildings to treaties, organizations and computer systems.
items.cn: 这个词从建筑扩展到条约、组织与计算机系统。
