definition_zh: 隧道；地道；坑道；挖隧道；凿通
definition_en: a long underground passage dug through a hill, under a city or under the sea, or to dig such a passage
core_image: 在大山或海底里打洞，让道路笔直穿过去
scene: 山体挡住了新公路的去路，工程队决定直接从山腹里穿过去。 The workers began to tunnel through the mountain last spring.
sceneCN: 这里 tunnel 是动词「挖隧道、凿通」（第 5 个义项：挖掘穿越通道）；句意为工人们去年春天开始在这座山中挖隧道。

pos.zh: 动词：挖隧道；凿通；在……下面挖通道

collocations.phrase: light at the end of the tunnel
collocations.zh: 苦尽甘来的迹象；隧道尽头的光明

derivatives.zh: 由本词加表示施动者的后缀构成，义为「挖隧道的人（或动物）」，美国拼写常作 tunneler
由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「隧道工程；挖掘隧道（的行为）」

senses.title: A passage through a hill or mountain
senses.definition: an artificial underground passage dug through a hill or mountain for a road or railway
senses.definitionCN: 为公路或铁路在山体中开凿的人工地下通道
senses.example: The train slowed down as it entered the long tunnel.
senses.exampleCN: 火车驶入那条长隧道时减了速。
senses.why: The core image is a straight path pushed through what stands in the way; through a mountain, that path is a tube of stone.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是在阻挡之物中硬开出一条直路；在山体里，这条路就是一段石管。

senses.title: A passage under a city or road
senses.definition: an enclosed passage built under a city, a river or a busy road so that traffic can pass below
senses.definitionCN: 修建在城市、河流或繁忙道路之下，让车流从下方通过的封闭通道
senses.example: The subway tunnel runs beneath the busiest street in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 地铁隧道从这座城市最繁忙的街道下方穿过。
senses.why: The same tube moved under rivers and streets: the city sits on top, traffic flows inside.
senses.whyCN: 同一根管子移到了河流和街道之下：城市在上面，车流在管子里。

senses.title: A hollow passage in animals or plants
senses.titleCN: 动物的洞穴；昆虫的蛀道
senses.definition: a long narrow hole dug or bored by an animal or insect, such as a burrow or a track inside wood
senses.definitionCN: 动物或昆虫挖出的细长孔道，如地洞或木头里的蛀痕
senses.example: The beetle larvae left winding tunnels inside the wooden beam.
senses.exampleCN: 甲虫幼虫在木梁里蛀出了弯弯曲曲的孔道。
senses.why: Nature borrows the image: a narrow tube dug through earth or wood works just like the engineer's passage.
senses.whyCN: 自然借用了这一意象：在泥土或木头里蛀出的细管，与工程师的通道如出一辙。

senses.title: A tube in physics or engineering
senses.definition: a long enclosed tube used in engineering or physics tests, such as a wind tunnel for studying airflow
senses.definitionCN: 工程或物理试验用的封闭长管，如研究气流的风洞
senses.example: The car model was tested in a wind tunnel before production.
senses.exampleCN: 这款汽车模型在投产前经过风洞测试。
senses.why: A controlled tube becomes an instrument: air or particles are sent down the same kind of passage to be measured.
senses.whyCN: 受控的管道变成了仪器：让空气或粒子流过同样的通道以便测量。

senses.title: To dig an underground passage
senses.definition: to dig a long passage through earth, rock or under a structure
senses.definitionCN: 在泥土、岩石中挖掘，或在建筑物下方挖出一条长通道
senses.example: The prisoners tried to tunnel out of the old fortress.
senses.exampleCN: 囚犯们试图从这座古堡里挖地道逃出去。
senses.why: The noun turns into a verb: to make a tunnel is to tunnel, the picture stays one of pushing a tube through solid ground.
senses.whyCN: 名词转成动词：挖出一条 tunnel 就是 tunnel，画面始终是把一根管子推进坚实的地面。

senses.title: To force a way through resistance
senses.definition: to make a passage through something solid or through an obstacle, often by force or persistence
senses.definitionCN: 在实体或障碍中开出通路，常凭强力或坚持
senses.example: The miners tunnelled through a seam of hard rock.
senses.exampleCN: 矿工们凿穿了一层坚硬的岩层。
senses.why: The verb extends from earth to any solid barrier; the effort of boring through is the same.
senses.whyCN: 动词从泥土延伸到任何实体障碍；掘进的艰辛是一样的。

senses.title: Tunnel vision: a narrowed view
senses.definition: in the phrase tunnel vision, a mental state in which a person sees only one narrow part of a situation
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 tunnel vision，指只看见事物狭小一面的心理状态
senses.example: Fixating on quarterly numbers gives managers tunnel vision.
senses.exampleCN: 只盯着季度数字会让管理者陷入隧道视野。
senses.why: Inside a real tunnel you can only see the bright spot ahead; the metaphor borrows that narrowed field of sight.
senses.whyCN: 在真实隧道里只能看见前方亮点；这个比喻借用了那种变窄的视野。

senses.title: Light at the end of the tunnel
senses.definition: in the phrase light at the end of the tunnel, a sign that a long period of difficulty is nearly over
senses.definitionCN: 指短语「light at the end of the tunnel」，即漫长困难阶段接近尾声的迹象
senses.example: After two years of debt repayments, we finally see light at the end of the tunnel.
senses.exampleCN: 偿债两年之后，我们终于看到了苦尽甘来的迹象。
senses.why: The image again looks down a long passage: hope is the spot of daylight growing at the far end.
senses.whyCN: 意象仍来自望向长长通道的尽头：希望就是远处越来越亮的日光。

intro.en: Tunnel goes back to a French word for a barrel; the passage got its name from the shape of a cask.
intro.cn: tunnel 可追溯到一个表示「大酒桶」的法语词；通道之名正来自酒桶的形状。

items.en: Old French tonel meant 'cask, barrel'; its earlier origin is generally considered to be uncertain, possibly of Gaulish or Germanic source.
items.cn: 古法语 tonel 意为「桶、大酒桶」；其更早来源一般认为不确定，可能有高卢语或日耳曼语源头。

items.en: French tonnelle meant 'a tun-shaped net' and later an arched arbour; the tube-like shape is central to the family.
items.cn: 法语 tonnelle 意为「桶形网」，后来也指拱形花架；管状外形是整个词族的核心。

items.en: English took the word in the fifteenth century for a net shaped like a tun; a tun is a large wine barrel.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入该词，指形状如大酒桶的网；tun 即大酒桶。

items.en: The canal builders of the eighteenth century applied the barrel shape to underground passages, and the modern sense was born.
items.cn: 十八世纪开凿运河的工程师把酒桶之形移用到地下通道上，现代义项由此诞生。

items.en: Railway engineering spread the word worldwide; the verb and the phrase tunnel vision followed in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 十九世纪铁路工程把这个词传遍世界；动词和短语 tunnel vision 在二十世纪相继出现。

items.en: Today the word covers railway, road, animal and figurative passages alike.
items.cn: 如今这个词同时涵盖铁路、公路、动物洞穴和比喻义的通道。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the barrel root; the near-meaning group gathers passages, burrows and related digging words.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「桶」词根构成的一族词；近义组收通道、洞穴及相关挖掘词。

entries.definition: A large cask for wine or beer, and an old unit of capacity; the shape that named the tunnel.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「大酒桶」，兼指旧容量单位；正是它的形状给 tunnel 命名。

entries.definition: An old Spanish and Portuguese unit of weight or capacity, historically tied to a barrel load; spelled similarly and sharing the barrel idea.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指旧时西班牙、葡萄牙的重量或容量单位，历史上与一桶货相关；拼写相近且同涉「桶」，但为另一语言分支的词。

entries.definition: A tube wide at one end and narrow at the other for pouring; it merely rhymes and looks alike, with an unrelated source.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「漏斗」，一端宽一端窄；只是音形与 tunnel 相近，词源无关。

entries.definition: The upper edge of the side of a boat; it looks like tunnel but comes from gunwale.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「船舷上缘」；形似 tunnel，实际来自 gunwale。

entries.definition: An informal blend of Channel and tunnel, once used for the cross-Channel link; now uncommon.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，Channel 与 tunnel 的非正式合成词，曾指跨海峡隧道，现已少用。

entries.definition: A hole dug by an animal for living, or to dig such a hole; natural rather than engineered.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「地洞；打洞」，指动物挖掘的住所，属自然行为而非工程。

entries.definition: A passage for people or traffic under a road or railway; usually shorter and open at both ends.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「地下通道；下穿道」，供行人或车流穿越道路下方，通常较短且两端敞开。

entries.definition: A natural hollow in rock; formed by nature, not dug by people for a route.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「山洞；洞穴」，为天然形成，并非人为开凿的通路。

entries.definition: To make a hole with a drill, especially a long one for tunnels or pipelines; names the digging act itself.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「钻、掘」，尤指为隧道或管道钻长孔，指挖掘动作本身。

entries.definition: In British English, an underground walkway; in American English, the underground railway itself.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，英式英语指地下行人通道；美式英语指地铁系统。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real barrel root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的「桶」词根，以及这个词实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: A tunnel is named after a tun, the great barrel: dig the cask sideways through a hill.
normal.cn: tunnel 得名于 tun（大酒桶）：把大酒桶侧过来从山里掏过去，就是隧道。

normal.en: The Channel Tunnel joins Britain and France under the sea.
normal.cn: 英吉利海峡隧道在英国与法国之间的海底相连。

normal.en: Wind tunnel tests how air flows past models of planes and cars.
normal.cn: 风洞测试飞机和汽车模型周围的气流。

normal.en: The verb keeps the image: tunnel through, tunnel under, keep digging.
normal.cn: 动词保留画面：tunnel through、tunnel under，不停地挖。

normal.en: Light at the end of the tunnel is hope after a long hard stretch.
normal.cn: 短语「light at the end of the tunnel」指漫长苦境之后的希望。

abstract.en: Picture a giant cask lying inside a mountain: hollow it out and a road runs straight through.
abstract.cn: 想象一根巨大的酒桶横卧山中：掏空它，一条公路笔直穿过。

abstract.en: Every tunnel is a promise of the other side; what feels endless is only long.
abstract.cn: 每条隧道都是对「彼端」的承诺；感觉无尽的东西只是很长而已。

abstract.en: Tunnel vision is looking down one tube and forgetting the sky above it.
abstract.cn: 隧道视野就是只盯着一根管子内部，忘了管子上方的天空。

examples.en: The new road tunnel shortens the journey across the mountains by an hour.
examples.cn: 新建的公路隧道把穿越群山的车程缩短了一小时。

examples.en: Rabbits tunnel deep into the sandy bank to make their burrows.
examples.cn: 兔子在沙质河岸深处打洞筑窝。

examples.en: At last we saw light at the end of the tunnel when sales began to rise.
examples.cn: 当销售额开始上升时，我们终于看到了隧道尽头的光明。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「探囊」——探囊取物般从山腹里掏出一条通道：隧道

root: 一般认为来自古法语 tonel「大酒桶」，更早源头不确定，可能有高卢语或日耳曼语背景；英语借入时指桶形渔网，十八世纪因外形相似转指地下通道，与 tun（大酒桶）同族。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses of tunnel all keep the barrel shape: passages through mountains and under cities, animal burrows, test tubes of air, and the verb that digs them, ending in two figurative looks down a long passage.
sensesIntro.cn: tunnel 的八个义项都保留酒桶之形：穿山与城市下的通道、动物洞穴、气流试验管道，以及挖掘它们的动词，最后是两个望向长长通道的比喻义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a giant barrel-shaped tube is hollowed straight through a mountain.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根巨桶状的管道被笔直掏空，穿山而过。

branches.en: THE WORKS: engineered passages carry roads and rails through and under obstacles.
branches.cn: 工程线：人工通道让公路与铁路穿山越河。

branches.en: THE NATURAL AND THE MEASURED: animals dig the same shape, and engineers seal it into an instrument.
branches.cn: 自然与测量线：动物掘出同样的孔形，工程师则把它封成仪器。

branches.en: THE ACT: the verb is boring the tube through whatever resists.
branches.cn: 动作线：动词就是顶着阻力把管子掘进去。

branches.en: THE MIND: standing inside the tube narrows what one can see.
branches.cn: 心智线：置身管中，视野随之变窄。

branches.en: THE PROMISE: looking down the long passage, the light at the end is hope.
branches.cn: 承诺线：望向长长通道尽头，那点光就是希望。

intro.en: Tunnel is built on the French barrel root tonel, and English adds ordinary suffixes and spellings around it.
intro.cn: tunnel 建立在法语「桶」词根 tonel 之上，英语再围绕它加上普通后缀和拼写变体。

latinIntro.en: The barrel word is French, not Latin, so there are no Latin cognates to list; the deeper origin is treated as uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 「桶」这个词来自法语而非拉丁语，故没有拉丁同族词可列；更早来源视为不确定。

items.example: The root gives the tube shape of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根赋予该词管筒之形。

items.example: It forms tonel, a small barrel-shaped thing.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 tonel，一个小小的桶状物。

items.example: Tunnelling names the act of digging.
items.exampleCN: tunnelling 指挖掘隧道这一行为。
tunneler 是挖隧道的人（或动物）。

items.example: The cousin word underpass also means under.
items.exampleCN: 近义词 underpass 同样含有「在下」之意。

items.example: It forms tunnel under, to dig beneath something.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 tunnel under，在下面挖通道。
它构成 tunnel vision（隧道视野）。

items.example: Machine boring is how modern tunnels are cut.
items.exampleCN: 机械掘进是现代隧道的开凿方式。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加施动者后缀构成，义为「挖隧道的人（或动物）」
由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「隧道工程；掘进作业」

definition_zh: 土壤；土地；弄脏
definition_en: the upper layer of earth where plants grow, a country's land, or to make something dirty
core_image: 双手捧起一把松软的深色泥土
scene: 这片土壤适合种蔬菜。 This soil is good for vegetables.
sceneCN: 这里 soil 是「土壤」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这片土壤适合种蔬菜。

derivatives.zh: 弄脏的
无土的

senses.title: Earth for plants
senses.definition: the upper layer of earth in which plants grow
senses.definitionCN: 植物生长所依赖的地表土层
senses.example: This soil is good for vegetables.
senses.exampleCN: 这片土壤适合种蔬菜。
senses.why: This is the basic agricultural sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的农业义项。

senses.title: Land of a country
senses.definition: the land of a country or region
senses.definitionCN: 一个国家或地区的土地
senses.example: The soldiers fought on foreign soil.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵们在异国土地上作战。
senses.why: The word widens from a patch of earth to a nation's ground.
senses.whyCN: 词义从一块土地扩展到一国的土地。

senses.title: Make dirty
senses.definition: to make something dirty
senses.definitionCN: 使某物变脏
senses.example: The muddy boots soiled the carpet.
senses.exampleCN: 泥靴子弄脏了地毯。
senses.why: A separate verb means to stain or dirty.
senses.whyCN: 一个单独的动词表示弄污或弄脏。

intro.en: Soil came from Old French and goes back to Latin solum, meaning ground.
intro.cn: soil 来自古法语，可追溯到拉丁语 solum，意为地面。

items.en: Solum meant ground, floor, or soil.
items.cn: solum 意为地面、地板或土壤。

items.en: Sueil or soil named a piece of ground.
items.cn: sueil 或 soil 指一块土地。

items.en: The word entered English as soil.
items.cn: 这个词以 soil 进入英语。

items.en: It named the earth in which plants grow.
items.cn: 它指植物生长的泥土。

items.en: A related verb came to mean making dirty.
items.cn: 一个相关动词发展为弄脏的意思。

note.en: Soil is compared with look-alike words and words for ground and earth.
note.cn: 把 soil 与形近词以及表示地面和泥土的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Soil is the thin living layer where roots and harvests begin.
normalIntro.cn: soil 是根系与收成开始的薄薄活土层。

normal.en: This soil is good for vegetables.
normal.cn: 这片土壤适合种蔬菜。

normal.cn: 士兵们在异国土地上作战。

normal.en: Rich soil holds water well.
normal.cn: 肥沃的土壤保水性好。

normal.en: Soil erosion threatens the hillside.
normal.cn: 土壤侵蚀威胁着山坡。

abstract.en: What we stand on is mostly invisible until it is lost.
abstract.cn: 我们脚下的东西大多在失去前都看不见。

abstract.en: Good soil is made by patience and decay.
abstract.cn: 好土壤由耐心和腐朽共同造就。

abstract.en: A country is more than the ground it claims.
abstract.cn: 一个国家不只是它宣称的土地。

dict_mnemonic.text: soil 与 soul、sole 形近；rich soil 是「肥沃的土壤」，soil erosion 是「土壤侵蚀」。

root: 经古法语来自拉丁语 solum（地面、土壤），核心义「植物生长的地表土层」。

sensesIntro.en: Soil is the earth where plants grow, a country's land, or the act of making something dirty.
sensesIntro.cn: soil 指植物生长的土壤、一国的土地，或弄脏某物。

core.en: The living ground under our feet.
core.cn: 我们脚下有生命的土地。

branches.en: Roots drink water from dark earth.
branches.cn: 根系从深色泥土中吸水。

branches.en: A nation claims a stretch of ground.
branches.cn: 一个国家宣称一片土地。

branches.en: Mud marks what it touches.
branches.cn: 泥巴在触到的东西上留下痕迹。

branches.en: A garden patch and a homeland share one word.
branches.cn: 花园地块与祖国大地共用一个词。

branches.en: Earth gives life and also stains.
branches.cn: 泥土给予生命，也会留下污迹。

intro.en: Soil builds words for rich ground, erosion, and clean or dirty states.
intro.cn: soil 构成表示沃土、侵蚀以及洁净或污渍状态的词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source solum means ground or floor.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语来源 solum 意为地面或地板。

items.example: The soil here is dark and rich.
Soilless farming uses water and minerals.

肥沃的土壤养出茁壮的植物。

items.meaning: soil able to grow good crops

latinEntries.example: Solum is the Latin source of soil.
latinEntries.exampleCN: solum 是 soil 的拉丁语来源。

definition_zh: 上面的；较高的；上部的；上游的；上层的；（地位）较高的
definition_en: higher in position or rank than something else
core_image: 两层抽屉，上面那层要抬手才够得着
scene: 书架从地面一直顶到天花板，最上面那几排书要搬梯子才拿得到。 The upper shelves are full of old magazines.
sceneCN: 这里 upper 是「上面的」（第 1 个义项：位置较高的）；句意为上面几层书架塞满了旧杂志。抬手才够得着的上层抽屉，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 由 upper 加 -most 构成，义为「最高的；最上面的」
upper 的比较级词尾所由来的原副词，义为「向上」
由 up 加 -wards 构成，义为「向上；朝上」

senses.title: Higher of two parts
senses.definition: higher in position when two parts are compared
senses.definitionCN: 比较两部分时位置较高的那一部分
senses.example: The upper drawer holds the knives.
senses.exampleCN: 上面那层抽屉放的是刀。
senses.why: The word is the old comparative of up, so it simply means the more up of two things.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 up 较古老的比较级，字面就是「两者中更靠上的那个」。

senses.title: Near the top of a building or body
senses.definition: used of the part of a building or a body nearer the top
senses.definitionCN: 形容建筑或身体靠近顶端的部分
senses.example: He lives on the upper floor of the old house.
senses.exampleCN: 他住在这栋老房子的楼上。
senses.why: A building is vertical, so the part nearer the roof is literally the more up part.
senses.whyCN: 建筑是竖着的，因此靠近屋顶的那部分字面上就是「更靠上的一端」。

senses.title: Higher in rank or class
senses.definition: used of people of higher social or official rank
senses.definitionCN: 形容社会或职务等级较高的人
senses.example: The upper class lived behind the park.
senses.exampleCN: 上层人家住在公园后面。
senses.why: Social rank is pictured as height, and the higher people are said to be in, the more the word applies.
senses.whyCN: 社会等级被画成了高度，人所在的位置越「高」，这个词就用得越贴切。

senses.title: Further up a river
senses.definition: used of the part of a river further from the sea
senses.definitionCN: 形容河流离海较远的一段
senses.example: They swam in the upper reaches of the river.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在河的上游河段游泳。
senses.why: A river runs downhill, so the higher part of the land gives the upper part of the stream.
senses.whyCN: 河往低处流，因此地势较高的那一段就成了溪流的上游。

senses.title: The higher of two limits
senses.definition: used of the highest figure allowed or recorded
senses.definitionCN: 形容允许或记录的最高数值
senses.example: The upper limit for the room is twenty people.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间的上限是二十人。
senses.why: Two bounds are compared exactly as two shelves are, and the higher one takes the word.
senses.whyCN: 两条界限的比较与两层架子的比较完全一样，较高的那条就用这个词。

senses.title: The top of a shoe
senses.definition: the part of a shoe above the sole
senses.definitionCN: 鞋底以上的部分
senses.example: The uppers are leather, the soles are rubber.
senses.exampleCN: 鞋帮是皮的，鞋底是橡胶的。
senses.why: The part of a shoe that rises above the sole is named by the same word that means the higher of two.
senses.whyCN: 鞋底之上升高起来的那部分，用的仍是表示「较高者」的这个词。

intro.en: The old comparative of up, kept as a separate adjective while the verb moved on.
intro.cn: up 的古老比较级形式，在其他用法继续演变时被保留为独立形容词。

items.en: The root upp means up, and a comparative form existed early in the family.
items.cn: 词根 upp 意为「向上」，这一语族很早就有了比较级形式。

items.en: The word yferra served as the comparative of up and meant higher.
items.cn: 古英语 yferra 充当 up 的比较级，意为「更高的」。

items.en: The form develops into upper, while up remains an adverb and particle.
items.cn: 这一形式后来发展为 upper，而 up 保持副词与小品词的身份。

items.en: Upper takes on social meaning in upper class and upper house.
items.cn: upper 在 upper class、upper house 中获得社会与制度义。

items.en: Concrete uses such as shoe uppers and upper limit keep the word physical.
items.cn: upper 也用于鞋帮、上限这类具体说法，保持着实感。

note.en: The look-alike group collects up- words and their compounds, while the near-meaning group compares words for height and rank.
note.cn: 形近组收集 up 系词及其复合词，近义组比较表示高低与等级的词。

definition_zh: 作业；任务；分配；指派；派驻；权利转让
definition_en: a piece of work given to someone, the act of giving it, a posting to a job or place, or the transfer of a right
core_image: 黑板上写着本周任务，每行后面跟着一个名字
scene: 教室黑板右角写着本周的阅读任务，几个名字被分到不同的小组。 The teacher gave us a writing assignment over the weekend.
sceneCN: 这里 assignment 是「作业、任务」（第 1 个义项：布置给学生的学习任务）；句意为「老师周末给我们布置了一篇写作作业」。画面中有黑板、任务清单与被分到各组的名字。

pos.zh: 名词：作业；任务；分配；指派；派驻；权利转让

derivatives.zh: assignment 的动词形式，义为「分配；指派；确定（时间、地点）」
由 assign 加 -ee 构成，义为「受让人；受托者」
由前缀 re- 加 assign 构成，义为「重新分配；改派」

senses.title: A piece of work given to someone
senses.definition: a piece of work, especially school work, given to a particular person to do
senses.definitionCN: 交给某个人去完成的一项工作，尤指学校作业
senses.example: The teacher gave us a writing assignment over the weekend.
senses.exampleCN: 老师周末给我们布置了一篇写作作业。
senses.why: The verb assign marked something out and handed it to a name; the noun is the thing so handed over.
senses.whyCN: 动词 assign 把某样东西划出来、交到一个名字名下；名词就是被交出去的那件事。

senses.title: The act of giving out work
senses.definition: the act of allocating a task, duty, or resource to a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 把任务、职责或资源分给某人或某组的行为
senses.example: The assignment of desks took longer than expected.
senses.exampleCN: 分配课桌花的时间比预想的长。
senses.why: This is the action side of the same word: the marking out and handing over itself.
senses.whyCN: 这是同一个词的动作面：划出与交出去这件事本身。

senses.title: A posting to a job or place
senses.definition: a job or period of work in a particular place, especially abroad or away from home
senses.definitionCN: 在某一地点、尤指海外或离家之外的工作或任职期
senses.example: She met her husband during an assignment in Kenya.
senses.exampleCN: 她在肯尼亚外派期间遇见了丈夫。
senses.why: A person is assigned to a place, so the posting itself takes the name of the assignment.
senses.whyCN: 人被分配到某个地方，于是这段派驻本身也承袭了 assignment 之名。

senses.title: The transfer of a right
senses.definition: in law, the transfer of a right or property from one person to another
senses.definitionCN: 法律上把某项权利或财产从一人转让给另一人
senses.example: The assignment of the lease required a signature.
senses.exampleCN: 租约的转让需要签字。
senses.why: Legally, a right is marked out from one owner and handed to another, just as a task is.
senses.whyCN: 在法律上，一项权利被从一个所有人名下划出、交到另一人名下，正如任务被交出去一样。

intro.en: Assignment is built on assign, which comes from a Latin phrase meaning to mark something out to someone.
intro.cn: assignment 建立在 assign 上，而 assign 来自一个拉丁短语，意为「把某物标记出来归于某人」。

items.en: Signum meant 'mark, sign', the word behind sign, signal and design.
items.cn: signum 意为「记号、标志」，是 sign、signal 与 design 背后的词。

items.en: Assignare, from ad- 'to' plus signare 'to mark', meant 'to mark out, allot, assign'.
items.cn: assignare 由 ad-「向」加 signare「标记」构成，意为「划出、分配、指派」。

items.en: In law the verb named the transferring of a right, a use that English kept.
items.cn: 在法律上这个动词指权利转让，这一用法被英语保留下来。

items.en: Old French assigner carried the task and property senses into English.
items.cn: 古法语 assigner 把任务义与财产义一并带入英语。

items.en: The noun assignment appears soon after the verb, first for a legal transfer and later for school work.
items.cn: 名词 assignment 紧随动词出现，先指法律转让，后指学校作业。

items.en: Modern use covers homework, shared duties, overseas postings and transferred rights.
items.cn: 现代用法涵盖家庭作业、分担的职责、海外派驻与转让的权利。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers nouns close to assignment in form; the near-meaning group gathers tasks, homework, missions and postings.
note.cn: 形近组收形式上与 assignment 接近的名词；近义组收任务、作业、使命与派驻。

entries.definition: The act of judging value or quality.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「评估、评定」，注意它与 assignment 词源不同。

entries.definition: A batch of goods sent for sale or delivery.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「寄售的一批货物」。

entries.definition: The state of being in line or in agreement.
A piece of work that must be done.
School work given to be done at home.
entries.definitionCN: 带回家完成的学校作业。

entries.definition: An important job given to a person or group, often abroad.
entries.definitionCN: 交给个人或团体的一项重要任务，常指海外任务。

entries.definition: A job in a particular place, especially abroad.
entries.definitionCN: 在某一地点、尤指海外的工作岗位。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow assignment from a name on a blackboard to school work, shared desks, an overseas post and a signed transfer.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子让 assignment 从黑板上的名字，走到学校作业、分课桌、海外派驻与签字的转让。

normal.en: Assignment: a task is marked out and a name is put beside it.
normal.cn: assignment：划出一项任务，在旁边写上一个名字。

normal.en: A writing assignment is the thing handed over.
normal.cn: 写作作业就是被交到手里的那件事。

normal.en: The assignment of desks is the handing over itself.
normal.cn: 分配课桌就是「交出去」这个动作本身。

normal.en: An overseas assignment is a posting to a place.
normal.cn: 海外派驻就是被分配到某个地方。

normal.en: A lease assignment hands a right to another name.
normal.cn: 租约转让把一项权利交到另一个名字名下。

abstract.en: One word names the task, the act, the post and the transfer.
abstract.cn: 一个词同时命名了任务、动作、职位与转让。

abstract.en: Everything assigned has been marked out for someone.
abstract.cn: 凡被 assign 的东西，都是为某个人划出来的。

abstract.en: School and law use the same handing-over gesture.
abstract.cn: 学校与法律用的是同一个「交出去」的动作。

examples.en: The teacher gave us a writing assignment over the weekend.
examples.cn: 老师周末给我们布置了一篇写作作业。

examples.en: The assignment of desks took longer than expected.
examples.cn: 分配课桌花的时间比预想的长。

examples.en: She met her husband during an assignment in Kenya.
examples.cn: 她在肯尼亚外派期间遇见了丈夫。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿赛门特」——阿赛门特在黑板上写下一行任务，再把名字填在后面：作业、指派

root: assignment 是 assign 加 -ment。assign 来自拉丁语 assignare「划出、分配」，由 ad-「向」加 signare「标记」构成，而 signare 又出自 signum「记号」。所以这个词的核心动作是「划出来、记到某个名字名下」：被划出来的那件事是作业或任务，划的动作本身是分配与指派，被划到某个地点是派驻，被划到另一个人名下则是法律上的权利转让。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses share one gesture of marking out and handing over: a task, the act of allocation, a posting, and a transferred right.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项共享同一个「划出来交出去」的动作：一项任务、分配的行为、一段派驻，以及转让的权利。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a blackboard listing this week's tasks, a name written beside each line.
core.cn: 核心意象：写着本周任务的黑板，每行后面都写着一个名字。

branches.en: THE TASK LINE: the thing handed to a person is the assignment.
branches.cn: 任务线：交到某人手里的那件事就是 assignment。

branches.en: THE ALLOTMENT LINE: the handing-over itself takes the same name.
branches.cn: 分配线：交出去这个动作本身也取同一个名字。

branches.en: THE POST LINE: a person assigned to a place serves there.
branches.cn: 派驻线：被分配到某地的人就在那里任职。

branches.en: THE LAW LINE: a right is marked out and given to another owner.
branches.cn: 法律线：权利被划出并交给另一个所有者。

branches.en: THE SCHOOL LINE: homework is both the thing given and the giving.
branches.cn: 学校线：作业既是被给出的东西，也是给出这件事。

intro.en: Assignment is assign plus -ment; its family adds -ee, the prefix re-, and the base sign words.
intro.cn: assignment 是 assign 加 -ment，词族再加 -ee、前缀 re- 以及 sign 一族词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin mark word signum also produced signal and design, both built on marking something out.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示记号的 signum 还生出 signal 与 design，两者都建立在「标出」这一动作上。

items.example: They assign each newcomer a mentor.

items.meaning: a person to whom something is transferred

items.exampleCN: 编辑把这则报道改派给别人了。

items.example: A red sign marked the exit.

items.meaning: a sign that carries a message
items.example: The lamp gave a warning signal.
items.exampleCN: 那盏灯发出了警告信号。

items.meaning: to plan and mark out a form
items.example: They design each page by hand.

latinEntries.example: The ship sent a signal for help.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 那艘船发出了求救信号。

latinEntries.example: The garden was designed for shade.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 这座花园是按遮阴来设计的。

definition_zh: 错误的；假的；不忠实的；虚伪的
definition_en: not true or correct; not genuine but made to look real; not loyal or sincere; based on a mistaken idea
core_image: 一件外表逼真、内里却空心的仿制品
scene: 那只是一场虚惊。 It was only a false alarm.
sceneCN: 这里 false 是「错误的、虚假的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：那只是一场虚惊。

derivatives.zh: 错误地；虚假地
虚假；不真实
谎言；虚假

senses.title: Not true
senses.definition: not true or correct
senses.definitionCN: 不真实或不正确的
senses.example: The rumour turned out to be false.
senses.exampleCN: 那个传言最终被证明是假的。
senses.why: The core sense is a statement that does not match facts.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是与事实不符的说法。

senses.title: Not genuine
senses.definition: not genuine but made to look real
senses.definitionCN: 并非真品，却做得像真的
senses.example: He gave a false name to the police.
senses.exampleCN: 他向警方报了假名。
senses.why: A copy pretends to be the real thing.
senses.whyCN: 仿制品假装是真品。

senses.title: Not loyal
senses.definition: not loyal or sincere toward someone
senses.definitionCN: 对某人不忠诚或不真诚
senses.example: A false friend leaves when trouble comes.
senses.exampleCN: 假朋友在麻烦来临时就会离开。
senses.why: A person can also be a hollow copy of a friend.
senses.whyCN: 一个人也可能是朋友的虚假复制品。

senses.title: Based on a mistake
senses.definition: based on a mistaken idea or wrong belief
senses.definitionCN: 建立在错误观念或错误信念上
senses.example: The locked door gave them a false sense of safety.
senses.exampleCN: 锁上的门给了他们一种虚假的安全感。
senses.why: A wrong belief is a false map of reality.
senses.whyCN: 错误信念是现实的假地图。

intro.en: False comes from Latin falsus, deceived or deceptive, from fallere, to deceive.
intro.cn: false 来自拉丁语 falsus（被欺骗的、欺骗性的），源头 fallere（欺骗）。

items.cn: 中古英语中 false 意为不真实与不忠。

items.en: False also describes artificial things.
items.cn: 现代英语中 false 也描述人造之物。

note.en: False means untrue; fault is a mistake or defect.
note.cn: false 是虚假的，fault 则是过错或缺陷。

normalIntro.en: False covers untrue claims, fake objects, disloyal people, and mistaken beliefs.
normalIntro.cn: false 涵盖不实说法、假货、不忠之人与错误信念。

normal.en: The story was completely false.

normal.en: She accused him of false promises.

normal.en: Test each statement as true or false.

abstract.en: Think of a friend who vanishes when needed.

examples.en: The witness gave false information.
examples.cn: 证人提供了虚假信息。

examples.en: He was accused of using a false passport.
examples.cn: 他被控使用假护照。

examples.en: Beware of false friends online.

sensesIntro.en: False means untrue, not genuine, disloyal, or based on a mistaken belief.

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a convincing shell with nothing real inside.

branches.en: The base sense is not matching the facts.
branches.cn: 基础义是与事实不符。

branches.en: A fake object pretends to be real.

branches.en: A disloyal person is a hollow friend.

branches.en: False words and false goods both deceive.

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 falsus、fallere 与 falsitas 解释了 false 及其词族。

items.example: They proved the falsity of the claim.
items.exampleCN: 他们证明了这个说法的虚假。

items.example: The fire was a false alarm.

items.meaning: a person who is not a true friend

definition_zh: 最终；最后；根本上；归根结底
definition_en: in the end, after everything has been considered, or at the most basic level
core_image: 绕了很大一圈之后落定的那一下
scene: 搬家的事商量了三个月，看过八处房子，最后还是定了最初那套。 Ultimately, they chose the small flat near the park.
sceneCN: 这里 ultimately 是副词「最终」（第 1 个义项：经过一切考虑之后）；句意为最终他们选定了公园附近那套小公寓。

pos.zh: 副词：最终；根本上；归根结底

derivatives.zh: 本词的形容词形式，义为「最终的；根本的」
同族名词，义为「最后通牒」

senses.title: In the end, after everything
senses.definition: after a long process or after all has been considered, as the final result
senses.definitionCN: 在漫长过程之后或一切考虑之后，作为最终结果
senses.example: The negotiations failed, and the deal ultimately collapsed.
senses.exampleCN: 谈判破裂，交易最终告吹。
senses.why: The adverb points to the end of the queue of events: whatever stands last is what truly happened.
senses.whyCN: 副词指向事件队列的末尾：站在最后的就是真正发生的。

senses.title: Fundamentally, at bottom
senses.definition: at the most basic level of causes or reasons
senses.definitionCN: 在原因或理由的最基本层面上
senses.example: The dispute was ultimately about water rights, not wages.
senses.exampleCN: 争端归根结底是关于水权，而非工资。
senses.why: Strip the surface layers and the deepest layer is what the sentence is really about.
senses.whyCN: 剥开表层，最深一层才是句子的真正所指。

senses.title: Tracing origins back to the source
senses.definition: used to say where something originally came from, through intermediate stages
senses.definitionCN: 用于说明某物经由中间阶段最初来自何处
senses.example: The word ultimately comes from a Greek verb for striking.
senses.exampleCN: 这个词最初源自一个表示「击打」的希腊语动词。
senses.why: The chain of borrowing runs backward until it stops; the stopping point is the ultimate source.
senses.whyCN: 借词链条一路回溯直至停下；停下的那点即终极来源。

senses.title: Ultimately responsible
senses.definition: in phrases about accountability, bearing the final responsibility that cannot be passed on
senses.definitionCN: 用于责任表述，指无法转嫁的最后责任
senses.example: The minister is ultimately responsible for the department's failures.
senses.exampleCN: 部长须为该部门的失误负最终责任。
senses.why: Responsibility climbs the hierarchy until someone at the top holds what remains.
senses.whyCN: 责任沿层级上行，直到顶层的人握住剩余的部分。

senses.title: What ultimately matters
senses.definition: in discussions of value, what counts most when everything else is set aside
senses.definitionCN: 在价值讨论中，撇开其余之后最重要的东西
senses.example: Rank and titles fade; what ultimately matters is trust.
senses.exampleCN: 头衔与级别都会褪色；最终要紧的是信任。
senses.why: Values too stand in a queue; the one at the end outlasts the rest.
senses.whyCN: 价值同样排成队列；站到最后的那个最长久。

senses.title: Eventually successful or settled
senses.definition: describing an outcome reached at last, often after setbacks
senses.definitionCN: 描述历经波折后终于达成的结果
senses.example: The rescue plan was ultimately successful, though costly.
senses.exampleCN: 救援计划终获成功，尽管代价高昂。
senses.why: The winding path is admitted, but its end is what the adverb seals.
senses.whyCN: 迂回之路被承认，但副词盖印的正是它的终点。

senses.title: The deciding turn in an argument
senses.titleCN: （论证中的）归根结底一锤定音
senses.definition: marking the final step of reasoning on which the conclusion rests
senses.definitionCN: 标出推理的最后一步，结论系于其上
senses.example: The data are suggestive, but ultimately only the trial can decide.
senses.exampleCN: 数据有启发意义，但归根结底只有试验才有决定权。
senses.why: Arguments are chains too; the adverb names the link that bears the conclusion.
senses.whyCN: 论证同样成链；副词所名的正是承受结论的那一环。

senses.title: Ultimately in historical narrative
senses.definition: in historical writing, the outcome toward which events moved
senses.definitionCN: 历史书写中，事件所趋向的终局
senses.example: The republic ultimately gave way to empire.
senses.exampleCN: 共和国最终让位于帝制。
senses.why: History is read backward from its end, so the narrative adverb naturally marks it.
senses.whyCN: 历史从其终点回读，叙事副词自然落在终局上。

intro.en: Ultimately is the ordinary English adverb of ultimate, with the Latin superlative underneath.
intro.cn: ultimately 是 ultimate 的普通英语副词形式，其下埋着拉丁最高级。

items.en: Latin ultimus meant 'farthest, last', the superlative shared by the whole family.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ultimus 意为「最远的、最后的」，是整个词族共享的最高级。

items.en: Medieval Latin ultimatus carried the sense of being brought to the last.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 ultimatus 带有「至于最后」之义。

items.en: The adjective ultimate entered English first, in learned and legal use.
items.cn: 形容词 ultimate 先进入英语，用于学术与法律语境。

items.en: The adverb ultimately followed, first meaning finally in a series, later also fundamentally.
items.cn: 副词 ultimately 随之出现，先表序列中的最终，后亦表根本上。

items.en: Science and philosophy extended it to ultimate causes and ultimate sources.
items.cn: 科学与哲学把它扩展到终极原因与终极来源。

items.en: Today it is a common connector in argument and narrative, marking the decisive end.
items.cn: 如今它是论证与叙事中常见的连接词，标出决定性的终点。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the ultimus family; the near-meaning group gathers finally, basically and at-last words.
note.cn: 形近组收 ultimus 词族；近义组收 finally、basically 等「终了、根本」类词。

entries.definition: The adjective from which this adverb is built.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，是构成本副词的基础。

entries.definition: A final proposal in negotiation; the family's last word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「最后通牒」，词族的最后一言。

entries.definition: Second to last; one step before the ultimate.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「倒数第二的」，比 ultimate 前一位。

entries.definition: Hidden and further in purpose, as in ulterior motive; another Latin comparative of the same base.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「别有用心的； further 的」，如 ulterior motive，是同一词基的拉丁比较级。

entries.definition: Beyond; prefix and word sharing the Latin base.
entries.definitionCN: 前缀兼单词，义为「超越」，与本词同出拉丁语词基。

entries.definition: In the end, after delay; stresses the time it took.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「终于」，强调所费的时间。

entries.definition: At the end, or to introduce a last point; lighter and more everyday.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「最后」，更轻快、更日常。

entries.definition: After waiting or effort; carries relief or impatience.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「终于」，带着如释重负或不耐烦。

entries.definition: At the basic level; overlaps with the root sense of ultimately.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「根本上」，与 ultimately 的根基义重叠。

entries.definition: When everything is finished; the plain phrase counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「到头来」，是本义最平实的对应说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real superlative root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的最高级词根，以及这个词实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: Ultimately is ultimate plus -ly: the adverb of the last thing.
normal.cn: ultimately 就是 ultimate 加 -ly：「最后之事」的副词。

normal.en: Ultimately responsible is the duty that stops with you.
normal.cn: ultimately responsible 是止于你身的责任。

normal.en: Word histories use ultimately from for the first source.
normal.cn: 词源叙述用 ultimately from 指出最初来源。

normal.en: But ultimately marks the point that outweighs the rest of the argument.
normal.cn: but ultimately 标出胜过其余论证的那一点。

normal.en: Ulterior motive is its Latin cousin: the purpose further behind.
normal.cn: ulterior motive 是它的拉丁近亲：藏在更深处的目的。

abstract.en: Watch a long discussion close: one sentence settles it, and that sentence is ultimately.
abstract.cn: 看一场长谈收尾：一句话定局，那句话就是 ultimately。

abstract.en: Every winding road has one final straight stretch.
abstract.cn: 每条迂回的路都有一段最后的直道。

abstract.en: Peel an onion fully and the small core is what remained ultimately.
abstract.cn: 把洋葱剥尽，最终剩下的就是那小小的芯。

examples.en: The project was delayed repeatedly but ultimately finished on budget.
examples.cn: 项目一再延期，但最终在预算内完成。

examples.en: Ultimately, the choice depends on what you value most.
examples.cn: 归根结底，选择取决于你最看重什么。

examples.en: The custom ultimately derives from an ancient harvest rite.
examples.cn: 这一习俗最终源自古代的收获仪式。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥缇默特利」——奥秘提到最后，默然特然利落定案：最终

root: 由 ultimate 加副词词尾 -ly 构成；ultimate 源自拉丁语 ultimus「最远的、最后的」（ulter 的最高级，与 ultra 同基），一般认为词基可溯至原始印欧语 *al-「生长、滋养」（重构形式）；同族词有 ultimatum、ulterior、penultimate 等。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses of ultimately all name the last point of a line: the end of events, the bottom of causes, the first source, the top of responsibility, the last value, the sealed outcome, the decisive step of an argument, and the end of a history.
sensesIntro.cn: ultimately 的八个义项都指一条线的最后一点：事件的终点、原因的底层、最初的来源、责任的顶端、最后的价值、盖印的结果、论证的决定一步，以及历史的终局。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: after a long winding path, one final point settles everything.
core.cn: 核心意象：长长的迂回之后，最后一个点定夺一切。

branches.en: THE END: outcomes reached, deals sealed, histories closed.
branches.cn: 终点线：结果达成、交易落定、历史收束。

branches.en: THE BOTTOM: basic causes and the decisive link of an argument.
branches.cn: 底层线：根本原因与论证的决定一环。

branches.en: THE SOURCE: tracing a chain back to its first link.
branches.cn: 溯源线：把链条一路回溯到最初一环。

branches.en: THE TOP: responsibility that can climb no further.
branches.cn: 顶端线：无法再上推的责任。

branches.en: THE VALUE: what remains when all else is set aside.
branches.cn: 价值线：撇开其余之后所剩的要紧之物。

intro.en: Ultimately joins the Latin superlative family with the plain English adverb ending.
intro.cn: ultimately 把拉丁最高级词族与朴素的英语副词词尾连在一起。

latinIntro.en: Latin ultimus and ultimatus are recorded; only the Indo-European base is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ultimus 与 ultimatus 均有记录；只有印欧词基属重构形式。

scene: 学校为新的图书馆筹集资金。 The school raised funds for a new library.

senses.title: Money kept for a purpose
senses.definition: an amount of money kept for a particular purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为特定目的保存的一笔钱
senses.example: The school raised funds for a new library.
senses.exampleCN: 学校为新的图书馆筹集资金。
senses.why: This is the main financial sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是主要的财务义项。

senses.title: A store of something
senses.definition: a large supply of something useful
senses.definitionCN: 大量有用的储备

intro.cn: fund 来自拉丁语 fundus，意为底部或地产。

items.en: Fundus meant the bottom or a piece of land.

items.en: It also named a source of income.
items.cn: 它也指收入来源。

items.en: Fund named money set aside for a purpose.

definition_zh: 不幸的；倒霉的；可惜的；令人遗憾的；不恰当的
definition_en: having bad luck, or being a regrettable thing to say or do
core_image: 刚出门就下雨，而伞恰好留在了家里
scene: 他赶到车站时，车门正好在眼前合上，下一班要等一小时。 It was an unfortunate start to the day.
sceneCN: 这里 unfortunate 是「倒霉的、不幸的」（第 1 个义项：运气不好）；句意为这一天的开头很不顺。刚出门就下雨而伞留在家里，正是这个词的核心画面。

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「不幸地；遗憾的是」
去掉否定前缀的形容词，义为「幸运的」
词族核心名词，义为「运气；财富」
用 mis- 表坏的近义词，义为「不幸；灾祸」

senses.title: Having bad luck
senses.definition: suffering from bad luck or a bad turn of events
senses.definitionCN: 遭遇坏运气或事态的不利转折
senses.example: The unfortunate passengers spent the night in the station.
senses.exampleCN: 那些倒霉的乘客在车站里过了一夜。
senses.why: The prefix negates fortune, which came from Latin fors, chance, so unfortunate means without good chance.
senses.whyCN: 前缀否定了 fortune（源自拉丁语 fors，机遇），unfortunate 就是没有好机缘。

senses.title: Regrettable rather than tragic
senses.definition: used of something mildly bad that one wishes had not happened
senses.definitionCN: 形容某件不太好、但愿没有发生的事
senses.example: It is unfortunate that the meeting falls on a public holiday.
senses.exampleCN: 会议恰逢公共假日，真是可惜。
senses.why: Bad luck on a small scale is simply a pity, so the word softens into regret.
senses.whyCN: 小尺度的坏运气就只是「可惜」，于是这个词软化成遗憾。

senses.title: Said of a person who deserves sympathy
senses.definition: used to describe someone who has been badly treated or badly served
senses.definitionCN: 形容受到苛待或委屈而值得同情的人
senses.example: He was unfortunate enough to be standing nearest the door.
senses.exampleCN: 他倒霉到刚好站在门边。
senses.why: Chance picks its victims without reason, and the word marks whoever chance picked.
senses.whyCN: 机遇挑人从不讲理由，这个词就标记出被挑中的那一个。

senses.title: Words or actions in poor taste
senses.definition: used of a remark or choice that is awkward and causes offence by accident
senses.definitionCN: 形容某句话或某个选择不巧令人不快，并非有意
senses.example: An unfortunate remark ruined the toast.
senses.exampleCN: 一句不恰当的玩笑毁掉了那番祝酒。
senses.why: A choice that brings bad consequences feels like bad luck even when it was your own.
senses.whyCN: 一个带来坏后果的选择，即使出于自己，也像坏运气一般。

senses.title: A combination of events that go wrong together
senses.definition: used of a coincidence or set of conditions that produce a bad outcome
senses.definitionCN: 形容若干条件凑在一起造成坏结果的巧合
senses.example: An unfortunate combination of wind and rain delayed the flight.
senses.exampleCN: 风雨不幸地凑在一起，让航班延误了。
senses.why: When several chances line up badly, the whole arrangement carries the label.
senses.whyCN: 当几个偶然凑得极糟，整个组合都带上了这个标签。

intro.en: Fortune comes from Latin through French, and English made the negative adjective with un-.
intro.cn: fortune 经由法语来自拉丁语，英语自己用 un- 造出否定形容词。

items.en: Fortuna was the goddess of chance, from fors, meaning luck or accident.
items.cn: Fortuna 是掌管机运的女神，出自 fors，意为「运气、偶然」。

items.en: Fortune entered French as a word for chance and what chance brings.
items.cn: fortune 进入法语，指机遇以及机遇带来的东西。

items.en: English borrowed fortune, which also came to mean wealth.
items.cn: 英语借入 fortune，后来又引申为财富。

items.en: Fortunate was formed from fortune, and un- was prefixed to it.
items.cn: fortunate 由 fortune 派生，再被加上前缀 un-。

items.en: The adjective softens into pity and mild regret in modern usage.
items.cn: 现代用法中，这个形容词软化为同情与轻微的遗憾。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the fortune family, and the near-meaning group gathers words of bad luck.
note.cn: 形近组是 fortune 词族，近义组汇集表示不幸的词。

normalIntro.cn: 这个词是带了否定前缀的 fortune，意思是机遇没有站在你这边。

normal.en: Un- plus fortunate: without good fortune.
normal.cn: un- 加 fortunate：没有好运。

normal.en: It is unfortunate that is the polite frame for bad news.

normal.en: An unfortunate remark points to awkward timing far more than to evil intent.

normal.en: Unfortunately is the sentence opener; unfortunate is the description.

normal.en: Fortune also means wealth, from the same idea of chance.
normal.cn: fortune 还表示财富，同出「机遇」这一观念。

abstract.en: Picture a bus doors closing as the runner reaches the stop.
abstract.cn: 想象跑者刚跑到站台，车门正好合上。

abstract.en: See a picnic blanket spread under a sky just breaking.
abstract.cn: 看野餐布铺开，天色却正要变坏。

abstract.en: Hear a joke land one word too late.
abstract.cn: 听一个笑话只差一个词就落空。

examples.cn: 这个不幸的家庭同时失去了房子和车子。

examples.cn: 遗憾的是没有人早点告诉她。

examples.en: An unfortunate choice of words turned a small dispute into a fight.

sensesIntro.cn: 把机缘好的一面去掉，从真正的困厄一直延伸到一句不巧的话。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an umbrella left at home just as the rain begins.
core.cn: 核心意象：刚下雨时，伞恰好留在家里。

branches.en: The luck branch: a person chance treated badly.
branches.cn: 运气分支：被机遇薄待的人。

branches.en: The pity branch: a small bad thing worth a sigh.
branches.cn: 惋惜分支：值得叹一口气的小坏事。

branches.en: The manners branch: words that sound wrong in the room.
branches.cn: 礼仪分支：在那个场合显得不妥的话。

branches.en: The coincidence branch: several conditions meeting badly.
branches.cn: 巧合分支：几个条件凑得极糟。

branches.en: The plain sense that most learners meet first.
branches.cn: 学习者最先遇到的最朴素义项。

intro.en: An English prefix sits on a noun that came through French from Latin.
intro.cn: 一个英语前缀压在一个经法语来自拉丁语的名词上。

latinIntro.en: The root of chance, fors, sits under Fortuna and gives the family its oldest layer.
latinIntro.cn: 表示「机遇」的词根 fors 藏在 Fortuna 之下，是这一族最古老的一层。
